definition_zh: 地形学的；地形上的；与地形测绘有关的；描写地貌起伏的
definition_en: relating to the shape and features of the land surface, or to maps and descriptions that record them
core_image: 测绘员站在雨后的山脊上，把每一道谷地与山头一笔笔画进带等高线的地图
scene: 测绘队在雨后的山脊上架起平板仪，把每一道谷地和山头画进等高线图。The topographical survey mapped every ridge and valley before the tunnel was designed.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（地形上的、地形学的）；句意为隧道设计之前，地形测量已把每一道山脊与谷地标注到图上。

pos.zh: 形容词：地形上的；地形学的；与地形测绘有关的；描写地貌的

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「地方」与「书写」两个成分加名词词尾构成，义为「地形；地形学；地形描述」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，与「地形上的」基本同义，技术文献中更常见
由名词加表示「从事者」的词尾构成，义为「地形测绘员；地形描述者」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在地形方面；从地形上看」
共享表示「地方」的第一个成分，加表示「名字」的成分，义为「地名」
由地名一词加学科名词词尾构成，义为「地名学」
共享表示「地方」的第一个成分，加表示「学问」的成分，义为「拓扑学」

senses.title: Relating to the shape of the land
senses.definition: concerning the physical relief of an area, its heights, slopes and depressions
senses.definitionCN: 指与某地区地表的起伏形态有关，包括高度、坡度与低洼处
senses.example: The topographical features of the valley decide where rain water collects.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地的地形特征决定雨水往哪里汇集。
senses.why: The Greek elements name a place and the act of writing it down, so the adjective first describes land that has been described.
senses.whyCN: 希腊成分一为「地方」、一为「书写」，因此这个形容词最初指「被描写下来的土地」。

senses.title: Belonging to a topographic map
senses.definition: shown on a map by contour lines, hachures or relief shading
senses.definitionCN: 指以等高线、晕滃或晕渲等方式表现在地图上
senses.example: The topographical map shows a steep drop beside the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 地形图上显示溪边有一处陡降。
senses.why: Once surveyors drew relief, the adjective moved from the land itself to the sheet that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 测量员把起伏画下来之后，这个词就从土地本身转到承载它的图纸上。

senses.title: Of regional anatomy
senses.definition: describing how structures are arranged within one region of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指描述身体某一区域内各结构的位置关系
senses.example: Topographical anatomy divides the neck into named triangles.
senses.exampleCN: 局部解剖学把颈部划分成若干具名三角区。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the mapping idea: a body region is charted like terrain.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了制图的想法：身体的一个区域也像地形一样被分区标注。

senses.title: Descriptive of a landscape in words
senses.definition: giving a detailed written account of the visible shape of a place
senses.definitionCN: 指用文字细致描写一个地方可见的形貌
senses.example: The novel opens with a topographical passage about the estuary.
senses.exampleCN: 小说以一段描写河口地貌的文字开篇。
senses.why: Writing a place down was the original meaning, and prose kept that literal sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 把地方写下来本是原义，散文让这层字面意思延续下来。

senses.title: Contrasted with political maps
senses.definition: showing natural relief rather than borders and administrative units
senses.definitionCN: 指表现自然起伏而非边界与行政单元
senses.example: A topographical map ignores provincial borders.
senses.exampleCN: 地形图不标省界。
senses.why: Surveying separated natural form from jurisdiction, and the adjective marks the natural side.
senses.whyCN: 测绘把自然形态与管辖范围分开，这个形容词标记的是自然那一面。

senses.title: Of terrain as a constraint
senses.definition: describing ground conditions that affect travel, construction or drainage
senses.definitionCN: 指影响通行、施工或排水的地面条件
senses.example: Topographical difficulties delayed the bridge by a full season.
senses.exampleCN: 地形上的困难使桥梁工程整整延期一季。
senses.why: Engineers treat terrain as a limit, so the adjective names the obstacle rather than the science.
senses.whyCN: 工程师把地形当作限制条件，于是这个词指障碍而非学科。

senses.title: Of relative height among peaks
senses.definition: in geography, describing the height of a summit above its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 地理学中指山峰高出周围地面的程度
senses.example: Topographical prominence decides whether a summit counts as a separate peak.
senses.exampleCN: 地形突出度决定一座山峰是否算作独立山峰。
senses.why: Relief is measured vertically as well as drawn horizontally, and prominence is the vertical reading.
senses.whyCN: 起伏除横向描绘之外还要纵向度量，突出度就是纵向读数。

senses.title: Figurative: the shape of a field of knowledge
senses.definition: used for the overall arrangement of ideas, as if they had heights and hollows
senses.definitionCN: 比喻思想观念的整体分布，仿佛它们也有高低起伏
senses.example: The lecture gives a topographical view of the whole debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座给出整场论争的版图式概览。
senses.why: Mapping moved from land to ideas, keeping the sense of an outline drawn from above.
senses.whyCN: 制图从土地移到观念，仍保留「从上往下勾出轮廓」的意思。

intro.en: Topographical joins Greek topos, a place, with graphein, to write or scratch, through the Latin noun topographia, a written description of a place. English took the noun as topography and added the adjective ending -ical.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把希腊语中表示「地方」的词与表示「书写、刻画」的词连在一起，经拉丁语中意为「对某地的文字描述」的名词进入英语；英语先借入名词，再加形容词词尾构成形容词。

items.en: Topos meant a place or a region, the spot that a speaker or writer points to.
items.cn: 这个词指一个地方或一片区域，即说话人或写作者所指的那一处。

items.en: Graphein meant to write or scratch, and it supplies the second half of many names of descriptive sciences.
items.cn: 这个词意为书写、刻画，是许多描述性学科名称的后半部分。

items.en: Latin combined the two Greek elements into a noun for a written account of a place; the term belongs to early modern Latin, and its first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 拉丁语把两个希腊成分合成一个名词，指对某地的文字记述；该词属于近代早期拉丁语，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: English adopted the noun first for the description of a district and later for the district's relief itself.
items.cn: 英语先借入这个名词指对某一地区的描述，后来指该地区的地形起伏本身。

items.en: The adjective spread with systematic surveying and was common by the nineteenth century; its precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词随系统测绘的兴起而扩散，到十九世纪已很常见，确切首见年份不确定。

items.en: Surveying, anatomy and engineering each took the adjective for the charting of their own ground.
items.cn: 测绘、解剖与工程各自借这个词来指称本领域「地盘」的图绘。

note.en: The first group shares the place element or the adjective ending; the second group names other ways of talking about the shape of the ground.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「地方」的成分或形容词词尾；第二组是谈论地面形态的其他说法。

entries.definition: The shorter adjective, preferred in technical writing, especially in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的形容词，技术写作中更常用，尤其在美国用法里。

entries.definition: The noun for the relief of an area or the study and mapping of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一个地区的起伏，或对它的研究与测绘。

entries.definition: A person who surveys and describes the surface of the land.
entries.definitionCN: 指测绘并描述地表形态的人。

entries.definition: A place name, built from the same first element with a word for name.
entries.definitionCN: 指地名，由同一个第一个成分与表示「名字」的成分构成。

entries.definition: The mathematical study of shape that survives stretching, with a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 数学中对拉伸后仍不变的形状性质的研究，第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: The variation in height of a land surface, the thing a topographic map draws.
entries.definitionCN: 指地表高低起伏的变化，正是地形图所绘制的内容。

entries.definition: The ground considered as a surface to cross or build on.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为通行或施工对象的地面。

entries.definition: A specific natural feature such as a ridge, valley or plain.
entries.definitionCN: 指山脊、谷地、平原等具体的自然形态。

entries.definition: Relating to the making and design of maps in general.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与地图制作与设计有关。

entries.definition: Relating to the scientific study of how landforms are formed.
entries.definitionCN: 指与研究地貌如何形成的学科有关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the two Greek elements: a place plus the act of writing it down.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着两个希腊成分展开：一个地方，加上把它写下来的动作。

normal.en: Place plus writing: topographical means the land has been written down.
normal.cn: 地方加书写：这个形容词的意思就是「土地被写成了图」。

normal.en: Contour lines are its signature look; a topographic map is relief made legible.
normal.cn: 等高线是它最典型的样子；地形图就是把起伏变得可读。

normal.en: A topographic map shows hills; a political map shows borders.
normal.cn: 地形图画出山丘，政区图画出边界。

normal.en: Topographical anatomy charts the body as if it were terrain.
normal.cn: 局部解剖学把身体当作地形来分区标注。

normal.en: Engineers list topographical difficulties when the ground itself is the problem.
normal.cn: 工程师列出的地形困难，指问题出在地面本身。

abstract.en: Every map is an argument about which features on the ground deserve to be drawn.
abstract.cn: 每一张地图都是一场争论：地面上哪些特征值得被画出来。

abstract.en: Relief is height turned into a language of lines.
abstract.cn: 起伏就是把高度翻译成一套线条语言。

abstract.en: To describe a place is already to choose a viewpoint above it.
abstract.cn: 描述一个地方，等于已经替它选好了一个居高临下的视角。

examples.en: The topographical survey mapped the flood plain before the dam was approved.
examples.cn: 大坝获批之前，地形测量已把洪泛平原测绘成图。

examples.en: Topographical maps show relief, not provincial borders.
examples.cn: 地形图表现起伏，不表现省界。

examples.en: Topographical anatomy helps a surgeon plan where to cut.
examples.cn: 局部解剖学帮助外科医生规划下刀的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「托坡格拉菲扣」——托着坡度、按格画线的一叠图，一张地形图：地形上的、地形学的

root: 希腊语 topos「地方」加 graphein「书写、刻画」，经拉丁语 topographia「对某地的记述」进入英语；形容词由名词加 -ical 构成，早期确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a place being written down to the map, the body, the building site and finally the shape of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「把地方写下来」出发，依次走向地图、身体、工地，最后落到论争的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surveyor on a wet ridge, drawing every hollow and summit onto a sheet of contour lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后的山脊上，测绘员把每一处低洼与山头画进一张等高线图。

branches.en: THE LAND DESCRIBED: spoken or written description of visible shape, the oldest use of the root.
branches.cn: 被描写的大地：对可见形貌的口头或书面描述，这是词根最古老的用法。

branches.en: THE MAP ITSELF: contour lines and natural features, set against borders and administrative units.
branches.cn: 地图本身：等高线与自然要素，与边界和行政单元相对。

branches.en: THE BODY AS GROUND: anatomy charts regions of the body the way a survey charts terrain.
branches.cn: 把身体当地面：解剖学像测绘地形那样标注身体分区。

branches.en: THE GROUND AS OBSTACLE OR MEASURE: terrain slows a project, and prominence ranks a summit.
branches.cn: 地面成为障碍或量度：地形拖慢工程，突出度给山峰排名。

branches.en: THE SHAPE OF IDEAS: a field of knowledge is described as if it had heights and hollows.
branches.cn: 观念的形态：一片知识被描述得仿佛也有高低起伏。

intro.en: Both halves of the word are Greek; Latin supplied the combined noun, and English added a compound adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都出自希腊语；拉丁语提供了合成名词，英语又加上了复合形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are borrowings of the Greek compound rather than native Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁形式是从希腊语借入的合成词，并非本土拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the first element in topography and toponym.
items.exampleCN: 它是「地形」与「地名」的第一个成分。

items.example: It supplies the second element in geography and biography.
items.exampleCN: 它是「地理」与「传记」的第二个成分。

items.example: It names a descriptive discipline or a style of writing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述性学科或书写体式的名称。

items.meaning: a written description of a place
items.example: The Latin noun carried both the place and the writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词同时带着「地方」与「书写」。

items.meaning: relief of an area; its mapping
items.meaningCN: 一个地区的起伏；对其测绘
items.example: English shortened and naturalised the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁名词缩短并本土化。

items.example: It forms topographical from topography.
items.exampleCN: 它由名词构成这个形容词。

items.meaning: one who surveys or describes terrain
items.example: The agent ending names the person who does the writing.
items.exampleCN: 表示施动者的词尾指从事这项书写的人。

items.example: The shorter ending is common in technical writing.
items.exampleCN: 较短的词尾在技术写作中更常见。

items.example: The second element means name rather than writing.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分意为「名字」而非「书写」。

items.meaning: study of shape under continuous change
items.meaningCN: 研究连续变化下形状性质的学问
items.example: The second element means study or discourse.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分意为「学问、论述」。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「地方」与「书写」加名词词尾构成，义为「地形；地形学」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「地形的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在地形方面」
由名词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「地形测绘员」
共享表示「地方」的成分，加表示「名字」的成分，义为「地名」
由地名一词加学科词尾构成，义为「地名学」
共享表示「地方」的成分，加表示「学问」的成分，义为「拓扑学」
由表示「地方」的希腊成分构成的构词成分，用于构成地点类术语

definition_zh: 构造板块；岩石圈板块；板块构造学说中的板块单元
definition_en: one of the large rigid pieces of the Earth's lithosphere that slowly move over the weaker mantle beneath
core_image: 球面上拼着许多厚石板，石板边缘相互顶住、错开，底下的软层缓慢流动
scene: 地质课上，教师把几张厚纸板拼成球面，演示坚硬的岩石圈如何裂成若干块并相互推挤。Each tectonic plate carries both crust and upper mantle and drifts on the softer rock below.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（岩石圈板块）；句意为每个构造板块都包含地壳与上地幔，并在下方较软的岩石上缓慢漂移。

pos.zh: 名词短语：构造板块；岩石圈板块；（板块构造学说中的）板块

derivatives.zh: 由希腊表示「建造」的词加形容词词尾构成，义为「构造的；地壳构造的」
由形容词加学科名词词尾构成，义为「构造地质学；构造作用」
由表示「扁平」的希腊词经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，义为「板；板块；盘子」
由「板块」与「构造学」组合而成，义为「板块构造学说」
由表示「微小」的前缀加「板块」构成，义为「微板块」
由「板块」加表示「边缘」的名词构成，义为「板块边缘」
由「板块」加表示「边界」的名词构成，义为「板块边界」

senses.title: A rigid slab of lithosphere
senses.definition: one of the large rigid pieces of the lithosphere, including crust and uppermost mantle
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石圈中一块巨大而坚硬的板块，包含地壳与上地幔顶部
senses.example: Each tectonic plate carries both crust and upper mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 每个构造板块都包含地壳与上地幔。
senses.why: The Greek builder word supplied the idea of a constructed slab, and the flat-sheet word supplied the shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语中表示「建造者」的词给出「拼装成的厚板」这一想法，表示「扁平」的词给出形状。

senses.title: One of the named major plates
senses.definition: one of the dozen or so large plates that geologists name, such as the Pacific plate
senses.definitionCN: 指地质学家逐一命名的十来块大板块，例如太平洋板块
senses.example: The Pacific tectonic plate is the largest of the named plates.
senses.exampleCN: 太平洋构造板块是具名板块中最大的一个。
senses.why: Once the mosaic was recognized, each piece needed a proper name for maps and papers.
senses.whyCN: 人们认出这幅拼图之后，每一块都需要在图件与论文里有正式名称。

senses.title: An oceanic plate
senses.definition: a plate whose upper part is dense basaltic oceanic crust
senses.definitionCN: 指上部由致密玄武岩质大洋地壳构成的板块
senses.example: An oceanic tectonic plate is thinner and denser than a continental one.
senses.exampleCN: 大洋构造板块比大陆板块更薄、更致密。
senses.why: Ocean floor rock is heavy enough to sink, so plates capped by it behave differently at the edges.
senses.whyCN: 洋底岩石足够重、会下沉，因此以它为顶的板块在边缘处表现不同。

senses.title: A continental plate
senses.definition: a plate whose upper part includes thick, buoyant continental crust
senses.definitionCN: 指上部包含厚实而较轻的大陆地壳的板块
senses.example: The continental tectonic plate rides higher on the mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆构造板块在地幔之上浮得更高。
senses.why: Continental rock is lighter, so the plate floats higher and resists subduction.
senses.whyCN: 大陆岩石更轻，因此板块浮得更高，也不易被俯冲。

senses.title: The edge zone where plates meet
senses.definition: the boundary zone along which two plates converge, diverge or slide past each other
senses.definitionCN: 指两块板块汇聚、分离或相互错动所经过的边界带
senses.example: Most earthquakes cluster along a tectonic plate edge.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数地震集中在构造板块边缘。
senses.why: The slab is rigid only in the middle; its rim is where all the friction and fracture happen.
senses.whyCN: 板块只有中部是刚性的，边缘才是摩擦与破裂集中发生的地方。

senses.title: The slow drift of a plate
senses.definition: the movement of a plate over the weaker mantle, usually measured in centimetres per year
senses.definitionCN: 指板块在较软弱的地幔之上移动，通常以每年若干厘米计
senses.example: The tectonic plate moves a few centimetres each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个构造板块每年移动几厘米。
senses.why: The word plate suggests something fixed, yet the whole point of the theory is that it travels.
senses.whyCN: 「板」这个词让人想到固定不动，而这套理论的要点恰是它在移动。

senses.title: A small independent plate
senses.definition: a small plate that moves separately within or beside a larger plate system
senses.definitionCN: 指在较大板块系统内部或旁边独立运动的小板块
senses.example: A small tectonic plate can rotate between two larger ones.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小构造板块可以在两个较大板块之间旋转。
senses.why: Finer surveying revealed pieces too small to appear on early world maps.
senses.whyCN: 更精细的测量揭示出早期世界地图上画不下的小块。

senses.title: A plate reconstructed for the past
senses.definition: a plate that existed in the geological past and is reconstructed from fragments
senses.definitionCN: 指地质历史上曾经存在、由岩石碎片复原出的板块
senses.example: The ancient tectonic plate is known only from scattered fragments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老构造板块只能从零散碎片中推知。
senses.why: Old plates leave seams and fossils rather than outlines, so they must be pieced together.
senses.whyCN: 古老板块留下的是缝合带与化石而非轮廓，所以只能拼合复原。

senses.title: A unit in a classroom model
senses.definition: one piece of a simplified model used to demonstrate plate behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指演示板块行为时所用简化模型中的一块
senses.example: In the classroom model, each tectonic plate is a curved cardboard shell.
senses.exampleCN: 在课堂模型里，每个构造板块都是一片弯曲的纸板壳。
senses.why: The real slab is hundreds of kilometres thick, so teaching models shrink it to something cuttable.
senses.whyCN: 真实板块厚达数百公里，教学模型便把它缩小到可以剪裁的程度。

intro.en: Tectonic comes from Greek tekton, a builder or carpenter, through tektonikos, of building, and Latin tectonicus. English used it for architecture before geologists borrowed it for the building of the Earth's crust. Plate took a separate route from Greek platys, broad and flat, through a reconstructed Vulgar Latin form and Old French.
intro.cn: 「构造」一词来自希腊语中表示「建造者、木匠」的词，经表示「建造的」的形容词与拉丁语形式进入英语；英语先用它谈建筑，后来地质学家借它指地壳的拼装。「板块」另走一条路，从希腊语表示「宽而平」的词，经一种重构的通俗拉丁语形式与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Tekton meant a builder or carpenter, a craftsman who fits pieces together.
items.cn: 这个词意为建造者、木匠，即把构件装配起来的工匠。

items.en: The adjective described what belongs to building or construction.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述与建造、装配有关的事物。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective for things relating to building.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词，指与建造有关的事物。

items.en: English first used it in the seventeenth century for architecture; the geological sense arose in the nineteenth century, when the precise date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪先把它用于建筑；地质义在十九世纪出现，确切年份不确定。

items.en: Platys meant broad and flat; a reconstructed Vulgar Latin adjective supplied the later European words for a flat sheet.
items.cn: 这个词意为宽而平；一个重构的通俗拉丁语形容词提供了后来欧洲各语言中表示「平板」的词。

items.era: OLD FRENCH PLATE AND ENGLISH PLATE
items.en: Old French plate named a flat metal sheet, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century for flat dishes and sheets.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指扁平金属板，英语在十四世纪借入，指平盘与平板。

note.en: The first group shares the building root or the flat-sheet shape; the second group names other pieces and edges of the lithosphere.
note.cn: 第一组共享「建造」词根或「平板」形状；第二组是岩石圈其他块体与边缘的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for building or for crustal structure, used alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指「建造的」或「地壳构造的」形容词，可单独使用。

entries.definition: A flat sheet, dish or slab; the noun inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指平板、盘子或厚板，是短语中的名词。

entries.definition: A broad raised area of land with a flat top.
entries.definitionCN: 指顶部平坦的高地。

entries.definition: A flat decorative or memorial plate fixed to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指固定在表面上的扁平装饰板或纪念牌。

entries.definition: A large flat dish used for serving food.
entries.definitionCN: 指盛食物用的大平盘。

entries.definition: The technical synonym that names the layer the plate belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 技术同义词，点明板块所属的圈层。

entries.definition: A piece of crust considered as a unit, without the mantle part.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为整体看待的一块地壳，不含地幔部分。

entries.definition: The boundary zone at the edge of a plate.
entries.definitionCN: 指板块边缘的边界带。

entries.definition: A thick flat piece of solid material, the plain image behind the term.
entries.definitionCN: 指厚而平的一块固体材料，是该术语背后的朴素意象。

entries.definition: A small plate recognised within a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 指较大系统中被识别出的小板块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the builder and the flat board: a carpenter fitting large slabs into a curved shell.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「建造者」与「平板」展开：木匠把大块厚板装进一个曲面外壳。

normal.en: Builder plus flat sheet: a constructed slab, which is exactly what a plate is.
normal.cn: 建造者加平板：拼装成的厚板，正是板块的样子。

normal.en: The Pacific plate is the biggest piece in the mosaic.
normal.cn: 太平洋板块是这幅拼图中最大的一块。

normal.en: Oceanic plates are thin and heavy; continental plates are thick and light.
normal.cn: 大洋板块薄而重，大陆板块厚而轻。

normal.en: Earthquakes and volcanoes line the edges, not the middles.
normal.cn: 地震与火山沿边缘排列，而不是在板块中部。

normal.en: A classroom model cuts the shell into pieces you can hold.
normal.cn: 课堂模型把外壳剪成可以用手拿的块。

abstract.en: A rigid thing can still move, as long as everything beneath it is softer.
abstract.cn: 坚硬之物仍能移动，只要它下面的一切更柔软。

abstract.en: Most of the action in a system happens at its seams.
abstract.cn: 一个系统里的大部分动静都发生在接缝处。

abstract.en: Naming the pieces is how a theory turns a picture into a science.
abstract.cn: 给各块命名，是理论把一幅图变成一门科学的方式。

examples.en: Each tectonic plate moves on the mantle at about the speed a fingernail grows.
examples.cn: 每个构造板块在地幔上移动，速度约与指甲生长相当。

examples.en: The map colours every tectonic plate and marks the boundaries between them.
examples.cn: 这幅地图给每个构造板块上色，并标出它们之间的边界。

examples.en: A tectonic plate boundary is where most of the world's earthquakes occur.
examples.cn: 构造板块边界是世界大多数地震发生的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泰克托尼克·普雷特」——建筑师把扁平石板拼成球面，一块块都是构造板块：板块、岩石圈板块

root: 「构造」出自希腊语 tekton「建造者、木匠」，经 tektonikos「建造的」与拉丁语 tectonicus 进入英语，十七世纪先指建筑，十九世纪转指地壳构造；「板块」出自希腊语 platys「宽而平」，经重构的通俗拉丁语形式与古法语 plate 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one slab: the lithosphere piece, the named plate, its ocean or continent version, its edge, its drift, and its smaller and older relatives.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一块厚板展开：岩石圈中的那一块、具名板块、它的洋壳或陆壳版本、它的边缘、它的漂移，以及更小与更古老的同类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved mosaic of thick stone slabs, each pressed against its neighbours, floating on a softer layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅由厚石板拼成的球面拼图，每块都顶住邻块，浮在更软的一层之上。

branches.en: THE SLAB ITSELF: the rigid lithosphere piece, and the cut-down model used to teach it.
branches.cn: 厚板本身：坚硬的岩石圈块体，以及为教学剪小的模型。

branches.en: THE SIZES: the dozen named giants, and the small plates found between them.
branches.cn: 尺度之分：十来块具名巨板，以及夹在它们之间的小板块。

branches.en: THE TWO CRUSTS: heavy oceanic plates and buoyant continental plates.
branches.cn: 两种地壳：沉重的大洋板块与较轻的大陆板块。

branches.en: THE ACTIVE RIM: the boundary zone where plates meet, and the drift that carries them there.
branches.cn: 活动的边缘：板块相接的边界带，以及把它们送到那里的漂移。

branches.en: THE VANISHED PIECE: a plate known only from the fragments it left behind.
branches.cn: 消失的一块：只能凭遗留碎片推知的古老板块。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek building word to a Greek flatness word; Latin carried both into European languages.
intro.cn: 这条短语把一个希腊语「建造」词与一个希腊语「扁平」词连起来，拉丁语把两者带进欧洲各语言。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the building adjective from Greek, and a reconstructed Vulgar Latin adjective stands behind the flat-sheet word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入表示「建造」的形容词；表示「平板」的词背后是一个重构的通俗拉丁语形容词。

items.example: It supplies the first element of tectonic.
items.exampleCN: 它是「构造」一词的第一个成分。

items.example: It turned the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Latin passed the adjective to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词传给英语。

items.example: The geological sense is a nineteenth-century extension.
items.exampleCN: 地质义是十九世纪的延伸。

items.example: It forms the name of the discipline, tectonics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成学科名「构造学」。

items.example: It is the distant source of plate.
items.exampleCN: 它是「板块」一词的远源。

items.example: The form is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式是重构的，并非直接见于文献。

items.example: English took it for dishes and sheets of metal.
items.exampleCN: 英语借它指盘子与金属板。

items.example: The compound names the whole theory.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词指整套理论。

items.example: The prefix means small and the noun means plate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「小」，名词意为「板块」。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「建造」词加形容词词尾构成，义为「构造的」
由形容词加学科词尾构成，义为「构造地质学」
由希腊「扁平」词经拉丁语与古法语构成，义为「板；板块」
由「板块」与「构造学」组合而成，义为「板块构造学说」
由「微小」前缀加「板块」构成，义为「微板块」
由「板块」加「边缘」构成，义为「板块边缘」
由「板块」加「边界」构成，义为「板块边界」
由「构造」词干加表示作用的名词词尾构成，义为「构造作用」

definition_zh: 地震活动；地震活动性；震动活动；（引申）剧烈动荡
definition_en: the occurrence and level of earthquakes and ground shaking in a place, or a similarly violent upheaval
core_image: 深夜山谷里，地震仪的指针在滚筒纸上抖出一串锯齿，远处村舍的灯还亮着
scene: 深夜的山谷里仪器忽然抖动，值班员抓起记录纸核对震中位置。The seismic activity in the valley increased sharply after the dam began filling.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（地震活动）；句意为水库开始蓄水之后，谷地的地震活动明显增强。

pos.zh: 名词短语：地震活动；地震活动性；震动活动；（引申）剧烈动荡

derivatives.zh: 由希腊表示「地震」的词加形容词词尾构成，义为「地震的；地震引起的」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「地震活动性；地震频度」
由希腊「地震」词加学科词尾构成，义为「地震学」
由学科名加表示从业者的词尾构成，义为「地震学家」
由希腊「地震」词加表示「书写」的成分构成，义为「地震仪」
由希腊「地震」词加表示「测量」的成分构成，义为「地震计」
由希腊「地震」词加表示「记录」的成分构成，义为「地震图」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「无地震的；抗震的」

senses.title: Earthquakes in a region
senses.definition: the occurrence of earthquakes in a particular area over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 指某一地区在一段时间内发生的地震
senses.example: The region has recorded seismic activity for several centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区有记录的地震活动已持续数百年。
senses.why: The Greek word behind seismic means a shaking, so the phrase first counts shakings in a place.
senses.whyCN: 「地震的」背后的希腊词意为「震动」，因此这条短语首先是在数一个地方发生的震动。

senses.title: Ground motion recorded by instruments
senses.titleCN: 仪器记录到的地面震动
senses.definition: the shaking measured by seismometers, whatever its cause
senses.definitionCN: 指由地震计测到的地面震动，不论其原因
senses.example: Instruments log seismic activity around the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器昼夜不停地记录地震活动。
senses.why: Once sensors were installed, activity became a trace on paper rather than a story told by survivors.
senses.whyCN: 传感器装起来之后，活动变成了纸上的曲线，而不再是幸存者的叙述。

senses.title: Shaking caused by human operations
senses.definition: earthquakes or tremors triggered by mining, reservoir filling, injection or extraction
senses.definitionCN: 指由采矿、蓄水、注入或采出等人类作业触发的地震或震动
senses.example: Reservoir filling can trigger seismic activity far from the dam.
senses.exampleCN: 水库蓄水可能在离大坝很远的地方触发地震活动。
senses.why: Changing pressure underground can bring a fault closer to failure, so engineers track the response.
senses.whyCN: 改变地下压力会把断层推近破裂点，工程师因此追踪其反应。

senses.title: Shaking linked to a volcano
senses.titleCN: 与火山相关的地震活动
senses.definition: tremors produced by moving magma, gases or hot fluids beneath a volcano
senses.definitionCN: 指火山下岩浆、气体或热流体运动产生的震动
senses.example: Seismic activity beneath the volcano rose before the eruption.
senses.exampleCN: 火山喷发之前，其下方的地震活动增强。
senses.why: Magma breaking rock on its way up makes a signal that volcanologists read as a warning.
senses.whyCN: 岩浆上升时撑裂岩石，产生的信号被火山学家读作预警。

senses.title: A cluster or sequence of shocks
senses.definition: a swarm or sequence of small shocks concentrated in space and time
senses.definitionCN: 指在空间与时间上集中的一群小震或一串地震
senses.example: A swarm of seismic activity followed the main shock.
senses.exampleCN: 主震之后出现了一群地震活动。
senses.why: Activity is often counted as a sequence, because one shock raises the stress on its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 活动常按序列来统计，因为一次震动会抬高邻近断层的应力。

senses.title: Faint background shaking
senses.definition: low-level shaking detectable only with sensitive instruments
senses.definitionCN: 指只有灵敏仪器才能察觉的低强度震动
senses.example: Sensitive stations detect faint seismic activity deep below the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 灵敏台站能探测到地表深处的微弱地震活动。
senses.why: Quiet is relative: the ground is always moving slightly, and better tools keep finding more of it.
senses.whyCN: 「安静」是相对的：地面始终在轻微移动，工具越好就发现得越多。

senses.title: Controlled shaking in exploration
senses.titleCN: 勘探中的可控震源活动
senses.definition: shaking generated on purpose by explosions or vibrators and recorded to image the subsurface
senses.definitionCN: 指为给地下成像而有意用爆炸或振动器制造并记录的震动
senses.example: Exploration crews produce seismic activity to map rock layers.
senses.exampleCN: 勘探队制造地震活动，以绘制岩层分布。
senses.why: The same waves that damage a town can be used as a lamp shone into the ground.
senses.whyCN: 使城镇受灾的同一类波，也可以当作照进地下的灯。

senses.title: A level or intensity descriptor
senses.definition: a way of grading how much shaking a place or period has, from low to high
senses.definitionCN: 指用来分级描述某地或某时段震动多少的说法，从低到高
senses.example: Monitoring showed low seismic activity through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 监测显示整个冬季地震活动偏低。
senses.why: Administrators need a scale, so the phrase becomes a dial rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: 管理者需要一个刻度，于是这条短语变成一个读数而非一次事件。

senses.title: Figurative upheaval
senses.definition: a violent disturbance in politics, markets or an institution, compared to an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 指政治、市场或机构中的剧烈动荡，被比作地震
senses.example: The ruling caused seismic activity inside the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决在党内引起了剧烈动荡。
senses.why: Earthquake language lends itself to any shock that rearranges the landscape of a field.
senses.whyCN: 地震的语言适合形容任何重新排列某一领域格局的冲击。

intro.en: Seismic was coined in the nineteenth century from Greek seismos, an earthquake, which comes from seiein, to shake. The second word, activity, descends from Latin agere, to do or drive, through activus and French. The phrase therefore describes shaking that is going on.
intro.cn: 「地震的」一词在十九世纪由希腊语 seismos「地震」造出，后者来自 seiein「震动」。第二个词「活动」经拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」及其形容词形式与法语进入英语。整条短语说的就是正在发生的震动。

items.en: The verb meant to shake, to drive along or to agitate.
items.cn: 这个动词意为震动、推动或搅动。

items.en: The noun meant a shaking, and in ordinary use an earthquake.
items.cn: 这个名词意为震动，日常用法中指地震。

items.en: The adjective was formed in the nineteenth century for the study of earthquakes; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪为地震研究而造，确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Agere meant to do, to drive or to set in motion, the root behind action and agent.
items.cn: 这个词意为做、驱动、使运动，是「行动」与「施事者」等词的词根。

items.en: The adjective meant busy or given to action, and the noun named a state of being busy.
items.cn: 形容词意为忙碌的、好动的，名词指忙碌或活动的状态。

items.en: French carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, where it came to mean working or operating.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带进英语，时为十四世纪，义为运作、活动。

note.en: The first group shares the earthquake root; the second group names the events, the measurements and the smaller signals.
note.cn: 第一组共享「地震」词根；第二组是事件本身、测量结果与更细微的信号。

entries.definition: The adjective for earthquakes or for very large upheavals.
entries.definitionCN: 指地震的，或指极其巨大的动荡。

entries.definition: The frequency and distribution of earthquakes in a region.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区地震的频度与分布。

entries.definition: The scientific study of earthquakes and the waves they send out.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究地震及其所发出波动的学科。

entries.definition: The instrument that draws a permanent record of ground motion.
entries.definitionCN: 指把地面运动画成永久记录的仪器。

entries.definition: The trace produced by a seismograph.
entries.definitionCN: 指地震仪画出的那条曲线。

entries.definition: A single event of sudden ground shaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次突然的地面震动事件。

entries.definition: A small or continuous shaking, often a precursor.
entries.definitionCN: 指轻微或持续的震动，常为先兆。

entries.definition: The measured movement of the ground during shaking.
entries.definitionCN: 指震动过程中测到的地面运动。

entries.definition: A smaller shock following a larger earthquake.
entries.definitionCN: 指大震之后较小的震动。

entries.definition: A faint vibration of the ground, often from distant or human sources.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面的微弱振动，常来自远处或人为来源。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the shaking verbs and the instruments that turn shaking into a line.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「震动」的动词与把震动变成曲线的仪器展开。

normal.en: The root verb means to shake, so the phrase is simply shaking that is happening.
normal.cn: 词根动词意为震动，所以这条短语就是「正在发生的震动」。

normal.en: A seismograph turns the shaking into a jagged line on a drum.
normal.cn: 地震仪把震动变成滚筒纸上的一条锯齿线。

normal.en: Filling a reservoir changes pressure underground and can wake a fault.
normal.cn: 水库蓄水改变地下压力，可能把断层唤醒。

normal.en: Rising magma cracks rock, and that cracking is read as volcanic activity.
normal.cn: 上升的岩浆撑裂岩石，这种破裂被读作火山活动。

normal.en: Exploration crews shake the ground on purpose to see the layers below.
normal.cn: 勘探队有意震动地面，以看清下面的岩层。

abstract.en: The ground is never truly still; better instruments only make the restlessness audible.
abstract.cn: 地面从未真正静止，更好的仪器只是让这份不安变得可听见。

abstract.en: A single shock is an event; activity is a long conversation between faults.
abstract.cn: 一次震动是一个事件；活动则是断层之间的一场长谈。

abstract.en: Any field can be shaken, which is why earthquake words travel so easily.
abstract.cn: 任何领域都可能被震动，所以地震的词汇才如此容易借走。

examples.en: Seismic activity in the region has been monitored since the station opened.
examples.cn: 自台站启用以来，该地区的地震活动一直受到监测。

examples.en: Engineers link some seismic activity to fluid injection deep underground.
examples.cn: 工程师把部分地震活动与地下深处的流体注入联系起来。

examples.en: The report describes a steady rise in seismic activity before the eruption.
examples.cn: 报告描述了喷发之前地震活动的持续上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「赛斯米克·阿克提维提」——地一「赛」就抖，仪器立刻记下一笔，这就是地震活动：地震活动、震动活动

root: 「地震的」出自希腊语 seismos「地震」，源于 seiein「震动」，十九世纪加形容词词尾造出，确切年份不确定；「活动」出自拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」的形容词与名词形式，经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shake: the quakes themselves, the instruments that record them, their triggers, their swarms, their faint background, their uses, their scale and their figurative echo.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一次震动展开：地震本身、记录它的仪器、它的触发原因、成串的发生、微弱的背景、它的用途、它的等级，以及它的比喻回声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle trembling across a paper drum in a dark valley, writing a jagged line while the village sleeps.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷的黑夜里，指针在纸鼓上颤动，趁村庄沉睡时写下一道锯齿线。

branches.en: THE MEASURED EVENT: quakes happening in a region, and the scale used to grade them.
branches.cn: 被度量的事件：一个地区发生的地震，以及给它们分级的刻度。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENTAL VIEW: ground motion on a record, and the faint background only good tools hear.
branches.cn: 仪器视角：记录纸上的地面运动，以及只有好仪器才听得见的微弱背景。

branches.en: SHAKING ON PURPOSE OR BY ACCIDENT: injection and reservoirs, and controlled sources used as a lamp.
branches.cn: 有意或无意的震动：注入与水库，以及被当作灯用的可控震源。

branches.en: THE VOLCANIC SIGNAL: magma breaking rock on its way up.
branches.cn: 火山信号：岩浆上升途中撑裂岩石。

branches.en: FROM SWARM TO METAPHOR: a cluster of shocks, and any upheaval that rearranges a landscape.
branches.cn: 从震群到比喻：成串的震动，以及任何重排格局的动荡。

intro.en: The phrase is Greek for the shaking and Latin for the doing, a neat division between the event and the process.
intro.cn: 这条短语用希腊语说「震动」，用拉丁语说「进行」，正好把事件与过程分开。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplied the earthquake half; Latin supplied the activity half through its verb of doing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「地震」那一半，拉丁语通过表示「做」的动词提供了「活动」那一半。

items.example: It is the source of the first word.
items.exampleCN: 它是第一个词的来源。

items.example: The noun was built on this verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词由这个动词构成。

items.example: It forms the adjective seismic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「地震的」。

items.example: The adjective was coined in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在十九世纪造出。

items.example: It is the root of action, agent and activity.
items.exampleCN: 它是「行动」「施事者」「活动」的词根。

items.example: The adjective turned doing into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把「做」变成一种性质。

items.example: The noun named the state of being active.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指处于活动中的状态。

items.example: It forms activity from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成「活动」这个名词。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into a measurable property.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词词尾把形容词变成可度量的属性。

items.example: It forms the name of the recording instrument.
items.exampleCN: 它构成记录仪器的名称。

由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「地震活动性」

由「地震」词加「测量」成分构成，义为「地震计」

definition_zh: 水圈；地球上全部水体的总称；行星的水层
definition_en: the whole body of water on a planet, including oceans, ice, groundwater, lakes, rivers and atmospheric vapour
core_image: 教室里的透明地球仪上，蓝色薄膜从海面一直裹到云底，薄得像一层漆
scene: 教室里摆着一只透明地球仪，蓝色薄膜从海面一直包到云层底部。The hydrosphere includes the oceans, the ice caps, the groundwater and the water held in the air.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（地球上全部水体的总称）；句意为水圈包括海洋、冰盖、地下水以及悬浮在空气中的水。

pos.zh: 名词：水圈；地球全部水体；行星的水层

derivatives.zh: 由「水圈」加形容词词尾构成，义为「水圈的；水圈内的」
由希腊表示「水」的成分构成的构词成分，用于构成与水有关的术语
由希腊表示「球」的成分构成的构词成分，用于构成圈层名称

senses.title: All the water on Earth
senses.definition: the total mass of water on Earth, in every state and every reservoir
senses.definitionCN: 指地球上以各种状态存在于各处的全部水体
senses.example: The hydrosphere stores most of its water in the oceans.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈把大部分水储存在海洋里。
senses.why: The word names a sphere only because the total is imagined as one connected body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把它称作「球」，只是因为人们把全部水量想象成一个连通的整体。

senses.title: The water shell of the planet
senses.definition: the water layer viewed as a shell surrounding the solid Earth
senses.definitionCN: 指把水看作包在固体地球外面的一层
senses.example: The hydrosphere forms a thin, broken shell around the planet.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈在地球外面形成一层薄而不连续的外壳。
senses.why: Earth-system science divides the planet into shells, and water is one of them.
senses.whyCN: 地球系统科学把行星分成若干圈层，水是其中之一。

senses.title: A subsystem of the Earth system
senses.definition: the water component that exchanges matter and energy with the atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere
senses.definitionCN: 指与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈交换物质与能量的水的部分
senses.example: Water moves constantly between the hydrosphere and the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 水在水圈与大气圈之间不断移动。
senses.why: Once the shell is treated as a system, its exchanges with neighbouring shells become the main story.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把这层当作系统，它与相邻圈层的交换就成了主要故事。

senses.title: A planet's water inventory
senses.definition: the water held by another planet or moon, whatever its state
senses.definitionCN: 指另一颗行星或卫星所拥有的水，不论其状态
senses.example: The Martian hydrosphere is now mostly frozen or buried.
senses.exampleCN: 火星的水圈如今大多冻结或埋在地下。
senses.why: Planetary scientists extended the terrestrial term to any world with water.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学家把地球上的这个术语扩展到任何有水的天体。

senses.title: The slow reservoir of the water cycle
senses.definition: the part of the water system that stores water for a long time, especially groundwater and ice
senses.definitionCN: 指水系统中长期储存水的部分，尤其是地下水与冰
senses.example: Groundwater is the slowest part of the hydrosphere to renew.
senses.exampleCN: 地下水是水圈中更新最慢的部分。
senses.why: Storage time separates a reservoir from a channel, and the phrase covers both.
senses.whyCN: 储存时间把储库与通道区分开来，而这条术语两者都包括。

senses.title: The freshwater share
senses.definition: the small fraction of the total that is fresh rather than saline
senses.definitionCN: 指总水量中非咸水的那一小部分
senses.example: Only a small fraction of the hydrosphere is fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 水圈中只有一小部分是淡水。
senses.why: The whole is mostly salt water, so the useful part needs a separate label.
senses.whyCN: 整体大多是咸水，因此有用的那一小部分需要一个单独的说法。

senses.title: Water as a managed resource
senses.definition: the water system considered as a resource to be measured, allocated and protected
senses.definitionCN: 指被计量、分配与保护的水系统
senses.example: Engineers treat the hydrosphere as a resource with limits.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把水圈当作有限资源来对待。
senses.why: Resource language shifts the focus from description to allocation.
senses.whyCN: 资源语言把重点从描述转向分配。

senses.title: The water of a closed local system
senses.definition: the water contained in an isolated body such as a lake, a cave or a sealed basin
senses.definitionCN: 指湖泊、洞穴或封闭盆地等孤立水体中所含的水
senses.example: The cave's hydrosphere is cut off from the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这个洞穴的水体与地表隔绝。
senses.why: The same word scales down to any bounded volume of water.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能缩小到任何有边界的水体。

intro.en: Hydrosphere joins Greek hydor, water, with Greek sphaira, a ball, through the Latin form sphaera. The compound was coined in the nineteenth century as a parallel to atmosphere and later lithosphere; the precise coinage date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语中表示「水」的词与表示「球」的词组合起来，后者经拉丁语形式进入欧洲语言。这个合成词在十九世纪仿照「大气圈」造出，后来又有了「岩石圈」等并列词；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Hydor meant water, and its stem supplies the first half of hydrology, hydrate and hydrosphere.
items.cn: 这个词意为水，其词干构成「水文学」「水合物」「水圈」等词的前半部分。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or a globe, the shape of a celestial body.
items.cn: 这个词意为球、球体，即天体的形状。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as sphaera, which passed into the European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词，后来又传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English took the Latin noun for a round solid and later for any domain of activity.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，先指圆球体，后来指任何活动领域。

items.en: The compound was formed as a scientific parallel to atmosphere, naming the water shell of the planet.
items.cn: 这个合成词作为「大气圈」的科学类比而造，指地球的水层。

items.en: Twentieth-century Earth science made it one of several interacting shells, alongside atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere.
items.cn: 二十世纪的地球科学把它与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈并列，作为相互作用的圈层之一。

note.en: The first group shares the water or sphere element; the second group names neighbouring shells and water bodies.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「水」或「球」的成分；第二组是相邻圈层与具体水体的说法。

entries.definition: The air shell of a planet, coined with the same sphere element.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的空气层，用同一个「球」成分构成。

entries.definition: The rocky shell of a planet, built to match the water term.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的岩石层，按水的术语仿造。

entries.definition: The zone of life, another shell in the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 指生命存在的区域，同一族里的另一个圈层。

entries.definition: The scientific study of water, sharing the water root.
entries.definitionCN: 研究水的学科，共享「水」词根。

entries.definition: Half of a sphere, a word built with the same ball element.
entries.definitionCN: 指球的一半，用同一个「球」成分构成。

entries.definition: The circulation of water among ocean, air, land and life.
entries.definitionCN: 指水在海洋、大气、陆地与生物之间的循环。

entries.definition: An underground layer that stores and transmits groundwater.
entries.definitionCN: 指储存并输送地下水的地下岩层。

entries.definition: The area from which water drains into one river system.
entries.definitionCN: 指向同一河系汇水的区域。

entries.definition: A natural or artificial store of water.
entries.definitionCN: 指天然或人工的水储库。

entries.definition: The frozen part of the water system, ice and snow.
entries.definitionCN: 指水系统中冻结的部分，即冰与雪。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow water plus ball: a blue film wrapped around a globe.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「水」加「球」展开：一层裹住地球仪的蓝色薄膜。

normal.en: Water plus ball gives a water shell around a planet.
normal.cn: 水加球，就是行星外面的一层水壳。

normal.en: The ocean holds nearly all of it; ice, groundwater and vapour are the small shares.
normal.cn: 海洋占去几乎全部；冰、地下水与水汽只占小份。

normal.en: It sits beside atmosphere, lithosphere and biosphere in the same family of shells.
normal.cn: 它与大气圈、岩石圈、生物圈并列为同一族圈层。

normal.en: Groundwater is the slowest reservoir in the cycle.
normal.cn: 地下水是水循环中更新最慢的储库。

normal.en: Planetary scientists speak of a Martian hydrosphere, mostly frozen.
normal.cn: 行星科学家会说火星水圈，其中大部分已冻结。

abstract.en: A sphere is a way of seeing one connected thing where there are thousands of separate pools.
abstract.cn: 「球」是一种看法：把成千上万处分散的水看成一件连通的事。

abstract.en: Water is the part of a planet that keeps changing its address.
abstract.cn: 水是行星上不断更换住址的那一部分。

abstract.en: Every resource phrase begins as a description and ends as a budget.
abstract.cn: 每个资源说法都从描述开始，以预算告终。

examples.en: The hydrosphere exchanges heat with the atmosphere over every ocean surface.
examples.cn: 水圈在每一片海面上与大气圈交换热量。

examples.en: Most of the hydrosphere is salt water, so fresh water needs separate accounting.
examples.cn: 水圈的大部分是咸水，因此淡水需要单独核算。

examples.en: A planet's hydrosphere may be liquid, frozen or held as vapour.
examples.cn: 一颗行星的水圈可以是液态、冻结的，或以水汽形式存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「海德若斯菲尔」——海的水（海德）裹成一个球（斯菲尔），就是水圈：水圈、地球上的全部水体

root: 希腊语 hydor「水」加 sphaira「球」，后者经拉丁语 sphaera 进入欧洲语言；合成词于十九世纪仿「大气圈」造出，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat one blue film as total water, as a shell, as a system, as a planet's inventory, as storage, as freshwater, as a resource and as a sealed local pool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一层蓝色薄膜分别看作全部水量、一个圈层、一个系统、一颗行星的水量、储库、淡水、资源，以及局部封闭的水体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blue skin over a classroom globe, running from sea surface to cloud base.
core.cn: 核心意象：教室地球仪上的一层蓝色薄皮，从海面一直铺到云底。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND THE SHELL: all water at once, imagined as a layer around the solid Earth.
branches.cn: 整体与外壳：一次性看全部水，把它想象成包住固体地球的一层。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: water exchanging matter and energy with air, rock and life.
branches.cn: 系统：水与空气、岩石、生命交换物质与能量。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the same term extended to any planet's water.
branches.cn: 别的世界：同一术语扩展到任何行星的水。

branches.en: STORAGE AND THE USEFUL PART: slow reservoirs, and the small fresh fraction.
branches.cn: 储存与可用部分：缓慢的储库，以及那一小份淡水。

branches.en: FROM BUDGET TO BOUNDARY: water allocated as a resource, and water sealed inside a local body.
branches.cn: 从预算到边界：作为资源分配的水，以及封闭在局部水体中的水。

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound wearing a Latinised sphere; both halves are transparent and productive.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊合成词，只把「球」写成了拉丁化形式；两半都清楚且能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the form of the sphere word; the water element is Greek and has no native Latin root here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「球」这个词的书写形式；「水」的成分出自希腊语，此处没有本土拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the first element of hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它是「水圈」的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它是「水圈」的第二个成分。

items.example: Latin passed the form to later European languages.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形式传给后来的欧洲语言。

items.example: English uses it for both shapes and fields.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它指形状，也指领域。

items.example: It builds atmosphere, biosphere and hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「大气圈」「生物圈」「水圈」等词。

items.example: It builds hydrology, hydroelectric and hydrosphere.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「水文学」「水电」「水圈」等词。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin-derived ending to the compound.
items.exampleCN: 形容词给合成词加了源自拉丁语的词尾。

items.example: It is the Latin word for water, used in aquifer and aquatic.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语中表示「水」的词，用于「含水层」「水生」等词。

items.example: It is built on the same pattern with a Greek word for cold.
items.exampleCN: 它按同一模式加希腊语表示「寒冷」的词构成。

derivatives.zh: 由「水圈」加形容词词尾构成，义为「水圈的」
由希腊「水」成分构成的构词成分，用于构成与水有关的术语
由希腊「球」成分构成的构词成分，用于构成圈层名称
按同一模式由「寒冷」加「圈层」构成，义为「冰冻圈」

definition_zh: 岩石；石块；礁石；摇滚乐；摇晃；使震惊；困境
definition_en: a large mass of stone; a genre of popular music; to sway or to shock; a source of steady support or a state of difficulty
core_image: 海边悬崖上立着一块被浪打湿的巨石，远处舞台的灯已经亮起
scene: 海边悬崖上立着一块被浪打湿的巨石，远处舞台的灯已经亮起。A huge rock at the cliff edge splits the waves while music drifts from a distant stage.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（大块岩石）；句意为崖边一块巨石分开浪头，远处舞台传来音乐。

pos.zh: 名词：岩石；石块；礁石；摇滚乐；可靠依靠；困境
动词：轻轻摇晃；使剧烈震动；使震惊

derivatives.zh: 由「岩石」加形容词词尾构成，义为「多岩石的；像岩石般坚硬的」
由形容词加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「多岩石的状态」
由「摇晃」加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「摇椅；摇滚乐手」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「摇晃；摇摆」
由「岩石」与「落下」复合而成，义为「岩崩；落石」
由「底层」与「岩石」复合而成，义为「基岩；基本原则」
由「岩石」加表示场所的词尾构成，义为「岩石园」
由「摇晃」与「滚动」两个动词复合而成，义为「摇滚乐」

senses.title: A large mass of stone
senses.definition: a large natural mass of stone standing on or in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 指天然矗立在地面或地下的大块石头
senses.example: A huge rock at the cliff edge splits the waves.
senses.exampleCN: 崖边一块巨石把浪头分开。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the thing a landscape is built from, not a mineral sample.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指构成地景的整块东西，而非一块矿物标本。

senses.title: Stone as a material in geology
senses.definition: the solid mineral material that forms the crust, treated as a substance or a type
senses.definitionCN: 指构成地壳的固体矿物材料，被当作一种物质或类型
senses.example: This rock formed from cooled lava under the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这种岩石由海底冷却的熔岩形成。
senses.why: Geology turns the countable object into a substance, so the word gains a mass-noun life.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把可数的石块变成一种物质，这个词于是有了不可数用法。

senses.title: The solid layer beneath soil
senses.definition: the solid rock lying under soil or loose deposits, often called bedrock
senses.definitionCN: 指位于土壤或松散沉积物之下的坚固岩石，常称基岩
senses.example: The drill reached rock after two metres of clay.
senses.exampleCN: 钻机穿过两米黏土后触到基岩。
senses.why: Builders need a word for the point where loose ground ends and solid ground begins.
senses.whyCN: 建造者需要一个词，指明松散地面结束、坚固地面开始的位置。

senses.title: A named landmark of stone
senses.definition: a particular rock formation used as a landmark or a place name
senses.definitionCN: 指被当作地标或地名使用的某处岩石地貌
senses.example: The old rock is marked on every tourist map.
senses.exampleCN: 那块古老的岩石标在每一张旅游地图上。
senses.why: A single stone can anchor a whole landscape in memory and on maps.
senses.whyCN: 一块石头就能把一整片地景固定在记忆与地图上。

senses.title: Rock music
senses.definition: a genre of popular music with amplified instruments, a strong beat and a prominent guitar
senses.definitionCN: 指以电声乐器、强节奏与突出吉他为主要特征的流行音乐类型
senses.example: The band plays rock every Friday night.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队每周五晚演奏摇滚乐。
senses.why: The genre name is a twentieth-century shortening of an older phrase, not the stone word at all.
senses.whyCN: 这一类型名是二十世纪对旧短语的截短，与「石头」那个词并无关系。

senses.title: Rock and roll as an earlier style
senses.definition: the mid-century dance music from which modern rock developed
senses.definitionCN: 指二十世纪中期那种舞曲音乐，现代摇滚由它发展而来
senses.example: Rock began as dance music for a young audience.
senses.exampleCN: 摇滚起初是给年轻听众伴舞的音乐。
senses.why: The music sense came from the verb meaning to sway, which is what dancers did.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义出自表示「摇晃」的动词，舞者正是那样摇动。

senses.title: To sway gently
senses.definition: to move or cause to move slowly back and forth
senses.definitionCN: 指缓慢地来回摆动，或使某物这样摆动
senses.example: The empty boat rocked on the evening tide.
senses.exampleCN: 空船在晚潮上轻轻摇晃。
senses.why: This verb is native English and has nothing to do with the stone; it only shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是英语本族词，与石头无关，只是拼写相同。

senses.title: To shock deeply
senses.definition: to shake a person or an institution emotionally or politically
senses.definitionCN: 指在情感或政治上剧烈震动某人或某机构
senses.example: The verdict rocked the whole city.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决震动了整座城市。
senses.why: The swaying verb extends to the shaking of feelings, and then to any disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 表示摇晃的动词扩展到情绪的震动，再扩展到任何扰动。

senses.title: In serious difficulty
senses.definition: in the phrase on the rocks, describing a marriage, business or plan close to collapse
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「触礁」，形容婚姻、生意或计划濒临崩溃
senses.example: The company was on the rocks before the new investor arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新投资人到来之前，这家公司已濒临破产。
senses.why: A ship on rocks cannot move, and the image supplies a ready metaphor for a stalled venture.
senses.whyCN: 船触礁便无法移动，这个意象为停滞的事业提供了现成比喻。

senses.title: A dependable support
senses.definition: a person or thing that others rely on during difficulty, as in a rock of stability
senses.definitionCN: 指困难时期他人所依靠的人或事物，如「稳定的磐石」
senses.example: Her calm was a rock for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的镇定是全队的依靠。
senses.why: The stone image supplies weight and immovability, the two qualities people want in a supporter.
senses.whyCN: 石头的意象提供重量与不可移动性，这正是人们希望依靠者具备的两点。

intro.en: Rock is really three histories that share one spelling. The stone word came through Old French roche from a Vulgar Latin form of uncertain origin; the swaying verb is native Old English roccian; the music sense is a twentieth-century shortening of rock and roll, which grew out of the swaying verb.
intro.cn: 「岩石」这个词其实是三段共用同一拼写的历史。石头义经古法语进入英语，其更早的通俗拉丁语形式来源不确定；表示「摇晃」的动词是英语本族的古英语词；音乐义则是二十世纪对「摇滚」短语的截短，而那条短语又出自表示摇晃的动词。

items.en: A form meaning rock or cliff stood behind the Romance words; its own origin is uncertain, and some dictionaries suggest a pre-Roman source.
items.cn: 一个意为岩石或悬崖的形式存在于罗曼语各词背后；它本身的来源不确定，有些词典推测来自罗马统治之前的语言。

items.en: Old French roche named a rock or a cliff and carried the word north.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指岩石或悬崖，把词形带向北方。

items.en: Middle English rokke named a large stone, and the spelling settled as rock.
items.cn: 中古英语中这个词指大石块，拼写后来固定为现在的形式。

items.en: The native verb meant to move back and forth, and it survives in the swaying sense.
items.cn: 本族动词意为来回移动，其「摇晃」义保留至今。

items.en: The music phrase combined the swaying verb with roll, describing the motion of dancers; its first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 音乐短语把表示摇晃的动词与「滚动」组合，描述舞者的动作；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: From the nineteen-fifties the phrase was shortened to rock, which then named a whole family of styles.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代起，这条短语被截短为「摇滚」，随后指一整个风格家族。

note.en: The first group shares the spelling or a derived ending; the second group names stones, cliffs and the like.
note.cn: 第一组共享拼写或派生词尾；第二组是石头、悬崖一类的说法。

entries.definition: Full of rocks, or unsteady like a rocking motion.
entries.definitionCN: 指多岩石的，或像摇晃般不稳定的。

entries.definition: A curved support that allows rocking, or a rock musician.
entries.definitionCN: 指可摇晃的弧形支座，或摇滚乐手。

entries.definition: A garden built from stones and alpine plants.
entries.definitionCN: 指用石块与高山植物布置的岩石园。

entries.definition: A sudden fall of stones from a cliff.
entries.definitionCN: 指崖壁岩石突然坠落。

entries.definition: The mid-century dance music from which rock was shortened.
entries.definitionCN: 指二十世纪中期的舞曲音乐，「摇滚」由它截短而来。

entries.definition: A piece of hard mineral matter, the everyday word for what rock is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 指一块坚硬矿物质，是「岩石由什么构成」的日常说法。

entries.definition: A large rounded stone, especially one moved by ice or water.
entries.definitionCN: 指大块圆石，尤指被冰或水搬运过的。

entries.definition: A high steep face of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指高而陡的岩壁。

entries.definition: The solid rock under loose ground.
entries.definitionCN: 指松散地面之下的坚固岩石。

entries.definition: A rugged projecting mass of rock on a hillside.
entries.definitionCN: 指山坡上崎岖突出的岩体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations keep the three histories apart: stone, swaying and music.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把三段历史分开记：石头、摇晃、音乐。

normal.en: Stone came from Old French; sway came from Old English; music came from a dance phrase.
normal.cn: 石头义来自古法语，摇晃义来自古英语，音乐义来自一个舞蹈短语。

normal.en: Bedrock is the rock under the soil, the point a drill eventually reaches.
normal.cn: 基岩是土壤之下的岩石，是钻机最终触到的地方。

normal.en: A ship on the rocks cannot move, so the phrase means a stalled venture.
normal.cn: 船触礁便无法移动，所以这个短语指停滞的事业。

normal.en: A rock of stability is heavy and cannot be pushed over.
normal.cn: 「稳定的磐石」既沉重又推不倒。

normal.en: Rock music is played loud, but the word inside it began as a quiet sway.
normal.cn: 摇滚乐演奏得很响，但其中的词最初只是轻轻的摇晃。

abstract.en: One spelling can hide three unrelated pasts, and only the context chooses which one speaks.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写可以藏起三段不相干的过去，只有语境决定哪一段在说话。

abstract.en: Stone is the image of what cannot be moved; music is the image of what will not stand still.
abstract.cn: 石头是不可移动的意象，音乐是不肯静止的意象。

abstract.en: The same word can mean the ground beneath you and the force that shakes it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以指脚下的地面，也可以指撼动它的力量。

examples.en: The path was cut straight through solid rock.
examples.cn: 小路直接从坚硬岩石中开凿而过。

examples.en: She rocked the cradle until the child fell asleep.
examples.cn: 她摇着摇篮，直到孩子睡着。

examples.en: The scandal rocked the government within a week.
examples.cn: 丑闻在一周之内震动了政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「罗克」——一块大石头落地「咯」一声，也能指摇滚乐和摇晃：岩石、摇滚乐、摇晃

root: 石头义经古法语 roche 来自一个意为岩石或悬崖的通俗拉丁语形式，其最终来源不确定；摇晃义是古英语本族动词 roccian「来回移动」；音乐义是二十世纪对「摇与滚」短语的截短。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses divide into three families: the stone and its uses, the swaying and its emotional extension, and the music that borrowed the sway.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项分成三族：石头及其各种用法，摇晃及其情绪延伸，以及借用「摇晃」的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave-beaten boulder on a cliff, with a lit stage somewhere behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一块被浪打的巨石，身后远处有一处亮灯的舞台。

branches.en: THE GROUND: a mass of stone, the material geology names, and the solid layer under soil.
branches.cn: 地面：一块巨石、地质学所称的材料，以及土壤之下的坚固层。

branches.en: THE NAMED STONE: one formation that anchors a landscape and a map.
branches.cn: 具名的石头：一处把地景与地图固定住的岩体。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: the modern genre and the earlier dance style it was cut from.
branches.cn: 音乐：现代类型，以及它被截短之前的早期舞曲风格。

branches.en: THE MOTION: gentle swaying, then the violent shaking of feelings.
branches.cn: 运动：轻柔摇晃，随后是情绪的剧烈震动。

branches.en: THE IMAGE OF STONE AT WORK: a stranded venture, and a supporter who cannot be pushed over.
branches.cn: 石头意象的两种用法：搁浅的事业，以及推不倒的依靠。

intro.en: The word has almost no internal structure; its interest lies in three separate origins and the endings built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词几乎没有内部结构，有趣之处在于三段各自独立的来源，以及由它们长出的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the stone line has a Latin-looking ancestor, and even that form is of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有石头这一条线有一个看似拉丁语的祖先，而这个形式本身的来源也不确定。

items.example: The form stands behind the Romance words for rock.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式是罗曼语各「岩石」词的背后来源。

items.example: Old French carried it into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把它带进中古英语。

items.example: The stone sense is the oldest noun use.
items.exampleCN: 石头义是最早的名词用法。

items.example: It is the separate source of the swaying verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是摇晃动词的另一来源。

items.example: The verb kept the motion and added the emotional sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留动作，又添了情绪义。

items.example: The phrase combined two verbs of motion.
items.exampleCN: 这条短语把两个表示动作的动词组合起来。

items.example: It forms rocky, full of rocks.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「多岩石的」这个形容词。

items.example: It forms rocker, a rocking support or player.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指摇椅或摇滚乐手的词。

items.example: It forms rockfall, a fall of stones.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指落石的词。

items.example: It forms bedrock, the rock under soil.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指基岩的词。

derivatives.zh: 由「岩石」加形容词词尾构成，义为「多岩石的」
由形容词加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「多岩石的状态」
由「摇晃」加施动者词尾构成，义为「摇椅；摇滚乐手」
由动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「摇晃」
由「岩石」与「落下」复合而成，义为「岩崩」
由「底层」与「岩石」复合而成，义为「基岩」
由「岩石」加场所词尾构成，义为「岩石园」
由「摇晃」与「滚动」复合而成，义为「摇滚乐」

definition_zh: 冰川作用；冰期；冰川覆盖；冰川地貌的形成
definition_en: the process or period of being covered by glaciers, and the landforms and record that ice leaves behind
core_image: 山谷里一条冰川退去后，裸岩上留下磨光的石面和成堆碎石
scene: 山谷里的冰川退去之后，裸岩上留下磨光的石面和成堆的碎石。Repeated glaciation polished the valley floor and left ridges of loose stone.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（冰川作用）；句意为反复的冰川作用把谷底磨光，并留下成脊的碎石。

pos.zh: 名词：冰川作用；冰期；冰川覆盖；冰川地貌的形成

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「冰」词加形容词词尾构成，义为「冰川的；冰期的」
由「冰川」词干加动词词尾构成，义为「使受冰川作用；冻结」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「受过冰川作用的」
由否定前缀加「冰川作用」构成，义为「冰川消退」
由表示「之间」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「间冰期的」
由拉丁「冰」词经法语进入英语，义为「冰川」
由「冰川」词干加学科词尾构成，义为「冰川学」

senses.title: The process of ice covering the land
senses.definition: the growth and spread of glaciers over a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 指冰川在陆地上生成、扩张并覆盖地面的过程
senses.example: Glaciation begins where snow lasts all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 在积雪整夏不化的地方，冰川作用开始了。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the action of ice into a process that can be observed and dated.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把冰的作用变成一种可观察、可测年的过程。

senses.title: A glacial period
senses.definition: a episode in Earth history when ice sheets expanded far beyond their present limits
senses.definitionCN: 指地球历史上冰盖远远超出当今范围的一段时期
senses.example: The last glaciation ended about eleven thousand years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 末次冰期约在一万一千年前结束。
senses.why: A process repeated many times becomes countable, and each episode gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程反复发生便变得可数，每一次都可以命名。

senses.title: The extent of ice cover
senses.definition: the area or share of a region that was covered by ice
senses.definitionCN: 指某一地区被冰覆盖的面积或比例
senses.example: The glaciation of the plateau reached its lowest slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 高原的冰川覆盖一直延伸到最低的山坡。
senses.why: Mapping turns the process into a boundary on a map.
senses.whyCN: 制图把这个过程变成地图上的一条界线。

senses.title: Landforms made by ice
senses.definition: the set of features produced by moving ice, such as U-shaped valleys, moraines and polished rock
senses.definitionCN: 指移动的冰所造成的一组地貌，如槽形谷、冰碛与磨光岩面
senses.example: The valley's glaciation is read from its polished walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这条谷地的冰川作用可从磨光的谷壁读出来。
senses.why: The word can name the results as well as the cause, because the results are what survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指原因也可指结果，因为留存下来的正是结果。

senses.title: The geological record of past ice
senses.definition: the evidence in rock, sediment and landform that ice once covered an area
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石、沉积物与地貌中留下的、说明某地曾被冰覆盖的证据
senses.example: Scratches on the bedrock record ancient glaciation.
senses.exampleCN: 基岩上的擦痕记录了古老的冰川作用。
senses.why: Once the ice is gone, only traces remain, and the word shifts to the traces.
senses.whyCN: 冰退去之后只剩痕迹，这个词便转向这些痕迹。

senses.title: Alpine glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation confined to mountain valleys, where ice flows down existing channels
senses.definitionCN: 指局限于山谷的冰川作用，冰沿原有河道下流
senses.example: Alpine glaciation carves sharp ridges and deep cirques.
senses.exampleCN: 高山冰川作用刻出尖锐山脊与深冰斗。
senses.why: Mountain ice is channelled, so the landforms it makes are narrow and steep.
senses.whyCN: 山地冰川受地形约束，因此造成的形态狭窄而陡峭。

senses.title: Continental glaciation
senses.definition: glaciation by broad ice sheets that bury the landscape rather than follow valleys
senses.definitionCN: 指由宽阔冰盖造成的冰川作用，冰盖掩埋地景而不沿谷地下行
senses.example: Continental glaciation flattened the whole plain.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆冰川作用把整片平原削平。
senses.why: An ice sheet ignores the valleys beneath it, producing a very different signature.
senses.whyCN: 冰盖不理睬下面的谷地，留下的印记因而完全不同。

senses.title: The cooling that accompanies ice growth
senses.definition: the climatic cooling and drying associated with expanding ice
senses.definitionCN: 指与冰体扩张相关的气候变冷与变干
senses.example: Early glaciation lowered temperatures across the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的冰川作用使整个大陆的气温下降。
senses.why: Ice both responds to climate and changes it, so the word carries a climatic echo.
senses.whyCN: 冰既响应气候又改变气候，这个词因此带上一层气候的回声。

intro.en: Glaciation rests on Latin glacies, ice, through the adjective glacialis and the Alpine word glacier. The noun with its process ending was formed in the nineteenth century, when geologists recognised that ice had once shaped whole landscapes; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语 glacies「冰」之上，经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯山区表示「冰川」的词进入欧洲语言。带过程词尾的名词在十九世纪形成，当时地质学家认识到冰曾经塑造整片地景；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, the solid form of water.
items.cn: 这个词意为冰，即水的固态。

items.en: The adjective meant icy or frozen, and it survives in the English word glacial.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为冰的、冻结的，英语中表示「冰川的」形容词由它而来。

items.en: Alpine French used a word for the moving ice of a valley, and English borrowed it in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 阿尔卑斯山区的法语用某个词指谷地中流动的冰，英语在十八世纪借入。

items.en: The adjective entered geology for ice and for periods of ice growth.
items.cn: 这个形容词进入地质学，指冰的或冰期扩张的。

items.en: Geologists added the process ending to name the action of ice on a landscape; the first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 地质学家加过程词尾，用来指冰对地景的作用；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century work dated successive ice advances and retreats, making the word countable and cyclic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究为一次次冰进与冰退测年，使这个词变得可数并带有旋回意味。

note.en: The first group shares the ice root or a derived ending; the second group names the periods, the ice bodies and the debris.
note.cn: 第一组共享「冰」词根或派生词尾；第二组是时期、冰体与碎屑的说法。

entries.definition: A mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley or across a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿谷地下行或横过大陆的缓慢移动冰体。

entries.definition: Relating to ice or to a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指与冰或冰期有关的。

entries.definition: To subject a landscape to the action of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指使地景受到冰的作用。

entries.definition: The retreat and melting of ice at the end of a glacial period.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰期结束时冰的退缩与融化。

entries.definition: A warmer interval between two glacial periods.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个冰期之间较温暖的间隔。

entries.definition: A long period when ice sheets were extensive.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰盖范围广大的漫长时期。

entries.definition: A single cold episode within an ice age.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个冰期内的一次寒冷阶段。

entries.definition: A broad dome of ice covering a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖大陆的宽阔冰穹。

entries.definition: Debris carried and dumped by a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰川搬运并堆积的碎屑。

entries.definition: Unsorted sediment left directly by ice.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰直接留下的未经分选的沉积物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the Latin word for ice and the marks ice leaves.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着拉丁语的「冰」词与冰留下的痕迹展开。

normal.en: Ice plus a process ending: the work ice does to a landscape.
normal.cn: 冰加过程词尾，就是冰对地景所做的工作。

normal.en: A U-shaped valley and polished walls are the signature of mountain ice.
normal.cn: 槽形谷与磨光的谷壁是山地冰川的标志。

normal.en: Scratches on bedrock outlive the ice that cut them.
normal.cn: 基岩上的擦痕比刻出它的冰活得更久。

normal.en: An ice sheet ignores valleys and flattens everything beneath it.
normal.cn: 冰盖不理睬谷地，把下面的一切削平。

normal.en: Repeated advances make the word countable: one glaciation, then another.
normal.cn: 反复的冰进让这个词可数：一次冰期，又一次冰期。

abstract.en: Ice is a sculptor that leaves its tools behind as rubble.
abstract.cn: 冰是一位雕刻家，把工具留成了碎石。

abstract.en: A process can be named twice: once as an event, once as the shape it left.
abstract.cn: 同一过程可以被命名两次：一次作为事件，一次作为留下的形状。

abstract.en: What melts away can still be read in what it scratched.
abstract.cn: 融化消失之物，仍能从它划过的痕迹里读出。

examples.en: Continental glaciation buried the plain under a sheet of ice.
examples.cn: 大陆冰川作用把平原埋在一片冰盖之下。

examples.en: The cirque is a classic landform of alpine glaciation.
examples.cn: 冰斗是高山冰川作用的典型地貌。

examples.en: Dates of past glaciation come from rocks and sediments.
examples.cn: 历次冰川作用的年代来自岩石与沉积物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「格拉西艾申」——格拉西（冰）把山谷磨光又退走，留下一个冰期：冰川作用、冰期

root: 拉丁语 glacies「冰」经形容词 glacialis 与阿尔卑斯法语表示「冰川」的词进入英语；带过程词尾的名词于十九世纪形成，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split the process from its episodes, its extent, its landforms, its traces, its mountain and continental styles, and its cooling effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把过程与其次序分开：过程本身、一次次冰期、覆盖范围、地貌、痕迹、山地与大陆两种样式，以及它带来的降温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a retreating glacier exposing polished rock and ridges of loose debris.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条退缩的冰川露出磨光的岩石与成脊的碎屑。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND ITS EPISODES: ice growing and spreading, then a named cold period.
branches.cn: 过程与阶段：冰生成、扩张，随后是一次具名的寒冷期。

branches.en: THE MAP: the area that ice covered.
branches.cn: 地图上的范围：冰曾经覆盖的区域。

branches.en: THE CARVING: landforms, in mountain valleys and under broad sheets.
branches.cn: 雕刻结果：山谷与冰盖之下形成的地貌。

branches.en: THE TRACES: scratches, sediment and erratics left after the melt.
branches.cn: 痕迹：融化后留下的擦痕、沉积物与漂砾。

branches.en: THE CLIMATE ECHO: cooling that accompanies the ice.
branches.cn: 气候回声：随冰而来的降温。

intro.en: The word is Latin ice with a process ending, plus a French word for the moving ice itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的「冰」加过程词尾，另有法语词指流动的冰本身。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun for ice and the adjective for icy; French supplies the name of the moving mass.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「冰」的名词与「冰的」形容词；法语提供流动冰体的名称。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整族词的词根。

items.example: It gives English glacial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语中的「冰川的」。

items.example: English borrowed it for valley ice.
items.exampleCN: 英语借它指谷地中的冰。

items.example: The verb ending marks the action.
items.exampleCN: 动词词尾标记这一作用。

items.example: It turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The adjective is used for both ice and periods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既指冰也指时期。

items.example: It forms the word for ice retreat.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示冰退的词。

items.example: It forms the word for warm intervals between ice ages.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示冰期之间暖期的词。

items.example: It forms glaciology, the study of ice.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「冰川学」。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「冰」形容词构成，义为「冰川的；冰期的」
由「冰川」词干加动词词尾构成，义为「使受冰川作用」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「受过冰川作用的」
由否定前缀加「冰川作用」构成，义为「冰川消退」
由「之间」前缀加形容词构成，义为「间冰期的」
由拉丁「冰」词经法语构成，义为「冰川」
由「冰川」词干加学科词尾构成，义为「冰川学」

definition_zh: 流域；河流盆地；以分水岭为界的汇水区域
definition_en: the whole area drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by divides
core_image: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢
scene: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢。A river basin gathers every drop that falls between its divides and carries it down one channel.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（流域）；句意为流域收拢分水岭之间的每一滴水，并把它送进同一条河道。

pos.zh: 名词短语：流域；河流盆地；汇水区域

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的；河岸的」
由「河流盆地」中的中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「范围广阔的」复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由表示「之间」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

senses.title: The area drained by one river system
senses.definition: all the land whose runoff reaches a single river and its tributaries
senses.definitionCN: 指径流最终汇入同一条河及其支流的全部陆地
senses.example: The river basin covers a fifth of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域覆盖全国五分之一的土地。
senses.why: The phrase starts as a shape on a map: everything that drains through one outlet.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语最初是地图上的一个形状：凡经同一出口排出的地方都算在内。

senses.title: A bowl-shaped lowland holding a river
senses.definition: a broad depression between higher ground through which a river and its tributaries flow
senses.definitionCN: 指高地之间、有河流及支流穿过的宽阔低地
senses.example: The river basin lies between two mountain chains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河流盆地位于两条山脉之间。
senses.why: The container word supplies the image of a bowl, and relief supplies the walls.
senses.whyCN: 「盆」这个词提供碗的意象，地形则提供碗壁。

senses.title: A unit of water management
senses.definition: the basin treated as one administrative unit for allocation, pollution control and flood planning
senses.definitionCN: 指把流域作为分配、治污与防洪规划的一个行政单元
senses.example: The river basin is managed by a single agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域由一家机构统一管理。
senses.why: Water crosses many jurisdictions, so managers redraw the basin as one budget line.
senses.whyCN: 水跨越许多辖区，管理者便把流域重画为一条预算线。

senses.title: A basin crossing political borders
senses.definition: a basin shared by two or more countries or provinces
senses.definitionCN: 指由两个或更多国家、省份共享的流域
senses.example: The river basin crosses three national borders.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域跨越三条国界。
senses.why: Water ignores borders, so the map unit and the political map rarely agree.
senses.whyCN: 水不理睬边界，因此流域单元与政区图很少吻合。

senses.title: A closed basin with no sea outlet
senses.definition: a basin whose water ends in an inland lake or evaporates rather than reaching the ocean
senses.definitionCN: 指水最终进入内陆湖或蒸发、而不流入海洋的流域
senses.example: The river basin has no outlet to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域没有通向海洋的出口。
senses.why: An enclosed basin is a bowl with no drain hole, and salts accumulate inside it.
senses.whyCN: 封闭流域像一个没有排水孔的碗，盐分因此在里面累积。

senses.title: A legal planning district
senses.definition: a basin defined by law for water-quality targets and permits
senses.definitionCN: 指为水质目标与许可证管理而依法划定的流域
senses.example: The river basin district must meet its water quality targets.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域区必须达到其水质目标。
senses.why: Regulation needs fixed lines, so the natural basin is redrawn as a legal district.
senses.whyCN: 监管需要固定界线，自然的流域因此被重画为法定区。

senses.title: A sedimentary basin filled by river deposits
senses.definition: a depression progressively filled with sand, mud and gravel brought by the river
senses.definitionCN: 指被河流带来的砂、泥与砾石逐渐填满的低地
senses.example: The river basin filled with sand and mud over millennia.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盆地历经千年被砂与泥填满。
senses.why: The bowl collects sediment as well as water, and geology reads the fill as a record.
senses.whyCN: 这个碗既收水也收沉积物，地质学把填充物读作记录。

senses.title: A region of shared water dependence
senses.definition: the community of users, farms and cities that depend on the same river system
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠同一河系的水的用户、农田与城市群体
senses.example: Farmers and cities in the river basin depend on the same snowmelt.
senses.exampleCN: 流域内的农民与城市依靠同一份融雪水。
senses.why: A basin is also a set of claimants, and the phrase can name them rather than the land.
senses.whyCN: 流域也是一群用水者，这个词因此可以指人而不指地。

intro.en: River came from Latin ripa, a bank, through the Vulgar Latin adjective riparia, land along a bank, and Old French rivere. Basin came through Old French bacin from Medieval Latin bacinus, a word of uncertain ultimate origin, possibly Gaulish.
intro.cn: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语形容词「沿岸的土地」与古法语进入英语。「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，其最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.en: Ripa meant the bank of a river, the edge rather than the water.
items.cn: 这个词意为河岸，指水边而非水本身。

items.en: The adjective named land along a bank, and it became the Romance word for a river.
items.cn: 这个形容词指沿岸的土地，后来成为罗曼语中表示「河流」的词。

items.en: Old French rivere carried the word into English as river.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，成为「河流」。

items.en: The word for a basin or bowl is of uncertain origin; a Gaulish source has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: 表示盆、碗的词来源不确定；有人提出高卢语来源，但未得到确证。

items.en: Old French bacin named a wide shallow vessel.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指宽而浅的容器。

items.en: English took the vessel word and later applied it to bowl-shaped land.
items.cn: 英语借入这个容器词，后来用它指碗状的地形。

note.en: The first group shares the river or basin element; the second group names the technical equivalents and the lines between them.
note.cn: 第一组共享「河流」或「盆地」的成分；第二组是技术同义词与它们之间的界线。

entries.definition: A bowl or a bowl-shaped area of land.
entries.definitionCN: 指盆、碗，或碗状的地形区域。

entries.definition: A large natural stream flowing to the sea or a lake.
entries.definitionCN: 指流入海洋或湖泊的大天然水道。

entries.definition: Relating to a river or its banks.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河流或其河岸有关的。

entries.definition: A smaller basin within a larger one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大流域内部较小的流域。

entries.definition: Extending across the whole basin.
entries.definitionCN: 指遍及整个流域的。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the area drained by a river system.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条河系所排水区域的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The area from which water is collected, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指集水区域，英国用法中常见。

entries.definition: In American usage the basin itself; in British usage the divide.
entries.definitionCN: 美国用法指流域本身，英国用法指分水岭。

entries.definition: The ridge of high ground separating two basins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分隔两个流域的高地脊线。

entries.definition: The flat land beside a river that floods periodically.
entries.definitionCN: 指河边周期性泛滥的平地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the bowl and the bank: water collected inside a rim and led out by one channel.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「碗」与「岸」展开：水被收在碗沿之内，再由一条河道送出。

normal.en: Think of a bowl: the rim is the divide, the bottom is the outlet.
normal.cn: 想一只碗：碗沿是分水岭，碗底是出水口。

normal.en: Everything inside the rim drains through the same river.
normal.cn: 碗沿以内的水都经同一条河流出。

normal.en: A closed basin is a bowl with no drain hole; salt stays inside.
normal.cn: 闭流流域是没有排水孔的碗，盐分留在里面。

normal.en: Water ignores borders, so a basin often crosses several countries.
normal.cn: 水不理睬国界，所以流域常跨越数国。

normal.en: A basin district is the legal redrawing of a natural bowl.
normal.cn: 流域区是把自然碗形改画成法定界线。

abstract.en: A catchment is a lesson in dependence: every slope sends its water to the same place.
abstract.cn: 流域是一堂关于依存的课：每道坡都把水送往同一处。

abstract.en: The same shape can be a physical bowl, a budget unit and a community.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状可以是物理的碗、预算单元，也可以是一个共同体。

abstract.en: Lines drawn on water are always negotiations, not facts.
abstract.cn: 画在水上的界线永远是协商，而不是事实。

examples.en: The river basin supplies water to more than thirty million people.
examples.cn: 这个流域为三千多万人供水。

examples.en: A transboundary river basin needs an agreement between the states that share it.
examples.cn: 跨界流域需要共享它的各州达成协议。

examples.en: Sediment cores show how the river basin filled over ten thousand years.
examples.cn: 沉积柱样显示这个盆地在一万年间如何被填满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞弗·贝森」——一条河被装进一只大碗（贝森），碗沿就是分水岭：流域

root: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语「沿岸土地」与古法语进入英语；「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat one catchment as a mapped area, a physical bowl, a management unit, a border case, a closed bowl, a legal district, a sediment trap and a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一片集水区分别看作地图区域、物理碗形、管理单元、跨界案例、封闭盆地、法定区、沉积陷阱与依存共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two tributaries meeting at a valley mouth, with a rim of hills holding the water in.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条支流在谷口相会，一圈丘陵像碗沿把水收住。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the drained area and the lowland that holds it.
branches.cn: 形状：被排水的区域，以及容纳它的低地。

branches.en: THE UNIT: a management area and a district fixed by law.
branches.cn: 单元：管理区域与依法划定的区。

branches.en: THE BORDER CASE: a basin shared by states that do not share a map.
branches.cn: 跨界案例：被不同国家共享、却不共享一张地图的流域。

branches.en: THE CLOSED BOWL: no outlet, so water and salt stay.
branches.cn: 封闭的碗：没有出口，水与盐都留下。

branches.en: THE FILL AND THE PEOPLE: sediment building the basin, and users sharing one snowmelt.
branches.cn: 填充与人：沉积物造出盆地，用户共享同一份融雪。

intro.en: One half names the bank, the other names the bowl; together they name a bowl of land drained by one river.
intro.cn: 一半说「岸」，一半说「碗」；合起来就是被一条河排水的一只陆地大碗。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the bank and the adjective of land along a bank; the bowl word reached Latin from an uncertain source, possibly Gaulish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「河岸」与「沿岸土地」的形容词；「碗」这个词进入拉丁语的来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.example: It is the source of river and riparian.
items.exampleCN: 它是「河流」与「河岸的」等词的来源。

items.example: It became the Romance word for river.
items.exampleCN: 它成为罗曼语中表示河流的词。

items.example: Old French passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把它传给英语。

items.example: The English word keeps the bank at its root.
items.exampleCN: 英语这个词的词根仍保留「岸」的意思。

items.example: It gave English basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语中的「盆地」。

items.example: Its ultimate source is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 其最终来源不确定。

items.example: English extended the vessel to land.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个容器词扩展到地形。

items.example: It forms subbasin, a smaller basin inside a larger one.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「子流域」，即大流域内的小流域。

items.example: It forms basinwide, covering the whole basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「全流域的」。

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的」
由短语中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由次级前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「遍及」成分复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由「之间」前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

definition_zh: 热带地区；南北回归线之间的地带；回归线
definition_en: the belt of the Earth between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, or the two circles that bound it
core_image: 正午太阳几乎直射，椰影缩成一小圈，河面升起白雾
scene: 正午太阳几乎直射，椰影缩成一小圈，河面升起白雾。The tropics receive nearly overhead sun at noon and stay warm through the year.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（热带地区）；句意为热带地区正午太阳几乎当顶，全年保持温暖。

pos.zh: 复数名词：热带地区；热带；南北回归线

derivatives.zh: 由复数形式还原为单数，义为「回归线；热带」
由「回归线」加形容词词尾构成，义为「热带的；炎热的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以热带方式；炎热地」
由表示「接近」的前缀加「热带」构成，义为「亚热带」
由表示「接近」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚热带的」
由同一「转向」词根加学科词尾构成，义为「向性；向性运动」

senses.title: The belt between the two tropics
senses.titleCN: 南北回归线之间的地带
senses.definition: the broad zone of the Earth lying between the two tropic circles
senses.definitionCN: 指地球上位于南北两条回归线之间的宽阔地带
senses.example: The tropics hold more species than any other belt.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地区拥有的物种比其他任何地带都多。
senses.why: The plural turns two boundary lines into the region they enclose.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把两条界线变成了它们所围住的区域。

senses.title: The two circles themselves
senses.definition: the two parallels where the sun is directly overhead at a solstice
senses.definitionCN: 指太阳在至日直射头顶的两条纬线
senses.example: The tropics are drawn at about twenty-three and a half degrees each side of the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 两条回归线画在赤道南北各约二十三点五度处。
senses.why: The circle is where the sun seems to turn back, and the plural can still name both lines.
senses.whyCN: 太阳在这条纬线上看似折返，复数形式仍可指这两条线。

senses.title: The hot wet climate zone
senses.definition: the climatic zone marked by high temperatures and heavy rainfall rather than seasons
senses.definitionCN: 指以高温与强降雨、而非四季变化为特征的气候带
senses.example: The tropics are warm in every month of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地区一年每个月都温暖。
senses.why: Climate classification took the geometric belt and gave it weather.
senses.whyCN: 气候分类把几何上的地帯赋予了天气特征。

senses.title: The rainforest biome
senses.definition: the forest ecosystems characteristic of the wet tropics
senses.definitionCN: 指湿润热带特有的森林生态系统
senses.example: The tropics store enormous amounts of carbon in living wood.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地区的活体木材储存着巨量碳。
senses.why: Ecology uses the region name for the biome that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用地名来指填满这片区域的生物群系。

senses.title: A farming region
senses.definition: the belt considered as a zone where particular crops can be grown
senses.definitionCN: 指被看作可种植某些作物的地带
senses.example: Coffee and bananas grow well in the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡与香蕉在热带地区长得很好。
senses.why: Trade maps crops onto climate belts, and the region name becomes an agricultural label.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把作物贴到气候带上，地区名于是成了农业标签。

senses.title: The zone of strongest sunlight
senses.definition: the latitudes that receive the most direct solar radiation through the year
senses.definitionCN: 指全年接受最直接太阳辐射的纬度带
senses.example: The tropics receive nearly overhead sun at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地区正午太阳几乎当顶。
senses.why: The old geometry of the turning sun survives as a statement about energy.
senses.whyCN: 太阳折返的古老几何，以能量说法延续下来。

senses.title: The belt of heavy rain and steady winds
senses.titleCN: 强降雨与稳定信风的地带
senses.definition: the zone influenced by the intertropical convergence and the trade winds
senses.definitionCN: 指受热带辐合带与信风影响的区域
senses.example: The tropics are marked by heavy rain and steady easterly winds.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地区以强降雨与稳定东风为标志。
senses.why: Atmospheric science fills the geometric belt with circulating air.
senses.whyCN: 大气科学用环流空气填满这个几何地带。

senses.title: The imagined lush elsewhere
senses.definition: a distant warm, green place as pictured by people who live outside it
senses.definitionCN: 指生活在别处的人所想象的温暖翠绿之地
