senses.example: Novels set in the tropics sell well in cold countries.
senses.exampleCN: 以热带为背景的小说在寒冷国家很畅销。
senses.why: Distance turns a climate zone into a scenery, and the plural carries that dream.
senses.whyCN: 距离把气候带变成一种风景，复数形式承载着这份想象。

intro.en: The word goes back to Greek trepein, to turn, and tropos, a turn. The tropic circles were named because the sun appears to turn back there at the solstices. Latin tropicus passed the adjective to English, and the plural came to name the whole region between the circles.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语 trepein「转动」与 tropos「转折」。两条回归线之所以得名，是因为太阳在至日前后看似在那里折返。拉丁语把形容词传给英语，复数形式后来指两条回归线之间的整片区域。

items.en: The verb meant to turn or to turn away.
items.cn: 这个动词意为转动、转向。

items.en: The noun meant a turn or a direction, and it also named a way of speaking.
items.cn: 这个名词意为转折、方向，也用来指说话的方式。

items.en: The adjective described what belongs to a turning, especially the turning of the sun.
items.cn: 这个形容词指与转折有关的事物，尤指太阳的折返。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective for the circles of the turning sun.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个形容词，指太阳折返的两条纬线。

items.en: English first used the singular for each circle, in texts on astronomy and geography.
items.cn: 英语最初用单数指每一条纬线，见于天文与地理文本。

items.en: The plural later shifted from the two lines to the belt between them; the precise date of that shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 复数形式后来从两条线转指它们之间的地带；这一转变的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the turning root; the second group names the zone by other conventions.
note.cn: 第一组共享「转折」词根；第二组用其他惯例称呼这个地带。

entries.definition: One of the two circles, or a region so described.
entries.definitionCN: 指两条回归线之一，或如此描述的地区。

entries.definition: The adjective for the tropics or for very hot conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指热带的，或指极其炎热的。

entries.definition: A figure of speech, from the idea of a turning of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指修辞格，源出「意义转向」的想法。

entries.definition: The turning of a plant or organism towards a stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物或生物朝刺激方向转动。

entries.definition: The warm belt just outside the tropics.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧邻热带之外的温暖地带。

entries.definition: The old name for the belt between the tropics, from Latin for scorched.
entries.definitionCN: 指两回归线之间地带的旧称，出自拉丁语「灼热」。

entries.definition: The band around the equator, the core of the tropics.
entries.definitionCN: 指赤道周围的带状区域，是热带的核心。

entries.definition: The latitudes near the equator, described by number rather than name.
entries.definitionCN: 指靠近赤道的纬度，以度数而非名称描述。

entries.definition: The dense wet forest typical of the humid tropics.
entries.definitionCN: 指湿润热带典型的茂密雨林。

entries.definition: The transition belts immediately poleward of the tropics.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧靠热带、向极地方向的过渡带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the turning sun and the belt it marks out.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着折返的太阳与它划出的地带展开。

normal.en: The sun turns back at the two circles, so the circles are called turning lines.
normal.cn: 太阳在两条纬线处折返，所以这两条线被称作转折之线。

normal.en: The plural turns two lines into the whole belt between them.
normal.cn: 复数形式把两条线变成它们之间的整片地带。

normal.en: Overhead noon sun means strong radiation all year.
normal.cn: 正午太阳当顶，意味着全年辐射强烈。

normal.en: Rainforest, coffee and bananas are the everyday pictures of the belt.
normal.cn: 雨林、咖啡与香蕉是这片地带最日常的画面。

normal.en: The old name Torrid Zone described heat rather than position.
normal.cn: 旧名「灼热带」描述的是炎热，而不是位置。

abstract.en: A line drawn for the sun becomes a place where people live.
abstract.cn: 为太阳画的一条线，最后成了人们生活的地方。

abstract.en: Naming a belt by its edges is always a simplification.
abstract.cn: 用地带边缘给地带命名，永远是一种简化。

abstract.en: Distance turns climate into scenery for those who never go.
abstract.cn: 对从未去过的人，距离把气候变成风景。

examples.en: Many crops grow faster in the tropics than in temperate zones.
examples.cn: 许多作物在热带地区比在温带长得更快。

examples.en: The tropics lose forest cover faster than any other region.
examples.cn: 热带地区失去森林覆盖的速度比其他任何地区都快。

examples.en: Explorers once feared the diseases of the tropics.
examples.cn: 探险者曾经害怕热带地区的疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「卓匹克斯」——太阳走到这里就「折返」，两条折返线夹出一片热带：热带地区、回归线

root: 希腊语 trepein「转动」与 tropos「转折」构成 tropos 的形容词 tropikos，经拉丁语 tropicus 进入英语；单数先指两条回归线，复数后指两线之间的地带，确切转变年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the bounded belt to the two lines, the climate, the forest, the farmland, the sunlight, the winds and the imagined elsewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从被围住的地带出发，依次走向两条界线、气候、森林、农田、日照、风系，以及被想象成的远方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a noon sun almost overhead, a palm shadow shrunk to a small circle and mist rising from a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：正午太阳几乎当顶，椰影缩成一小圈，河面升起白雾。

branches.en: THE GEOMETRY: the belt between the lines, and the two lines themselves.
branches.cn: 几何：两线之间的地带，以及两条线本身。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL ZONE: heat, heavy rain and steady trade winds.
branches.cn: 物理地带：高温、强降雨与稳定的信风。

branches.en: THE ENERGY VIEW: latitudes that receive the most direct sunlight.
branches.cn: 能量视角：接受最直接日光的纬度带。

branches.en: THE LIVING AND THE FARMED: rainforest and the crops that thrive there.
branches.cn: 生计与种植：雨林以及在那种植的作物。

branches.en: THE PICTURE FROM AFAR: a warm green elsewhere imagined by colder countries.
branches.cn: 远方的画面：寒冷国家想象中的温暖翠绿之地。

intro.en: The word is Greek for a turn, plus an adjective ending and a plural that turned a pair of lines into a region.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语的「转折」加形容词词尾，再加一个把两条线变成一片区域的复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective; there is no separate native Latin root here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词；此处没有另外的本土拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整族词背后的动词。

items.example: It also gives the word for a figure of speech.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成表示修辞格的词。

items.example: It was applied to the sun's turning circles.
items.exampleCN: 它被用来指太阳折返的纬线。

items.example: Latin passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把它传给英语。

items.example: The singular names one line.
items.exampleCN: 单数指一条线。

items.example: The plural shifted from two lines to the belt between them.
items.exampleCN: 复数从两条线转指两线之间的地带。

items.example: The adjective adds a Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词加了拉丁语词尾。

items.example: It forms tropical from tropic.
items.exampleCN: 它由「回归线」构成「热带的」。

items.example: It forms subtropics, the belt just outside.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「亚热带」，即紧邻之外的地带。

derivatives.zh: 由复数还原为单数，义为「回归线」
由「回归线」加形容词词尾构成，义为「热带的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以热带方式」
由「接近」前缀加「热带」构成，义为「亚热带」
由「接近」前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚热带的」
由同一「转向」词根加学科词尾构成，义为「向性」

definition_zh: 细胞膜；质膜；包裹细胞质的磷脂双分子层
definition_en: the thin barrier of lipid and protein that surrounds a cell and controls what enters or leaves
core_image: 显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边外停住
scene: 显微镜下，一枚细胞被荧光勾出细细的边，染料在边外停住。The cell membrane lets water through but keeps most dyes outside.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（细胞膜）；句意为细胞膜允许水通过，却把大多数染料挡在外面。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁表示「皮、膜」的名词构成，义为「膜；薄膜」
由「膜」加形容词词尾构成，义为「膜的；膜状的」
由拉丁表示「小室」的名词构成，义为「细胞；小室」
由「细胞」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞的；多孔的」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚细胞的」
由表示「在内」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「细胞内的」

senses.title: The boundary of a cell
senses.definition: the outer boundary separating the cytoplasm from the surrounding medium
senses.definitionCN: 指把细胞质与周围介质隔开的外边界
senses.example: Every cell membrane separates inside from outside.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层细胞膜都把内与外分开。
senses.why: A cell is a room, and a room needs a wall; the phrase names that wall.
senses.whyCN: 细胞是一间屋子，屋子需要墙，这条短语说的就是那面墙。

senses.title: The phospholipid bilayer
senses.definition: the double sheet of lipid molecules with their heads outward and tails inward
senses.definitionCN: 指脂质分子头朝外、尾朝内排成的双层薄片
senses.example: The cell membrane is a bilayer only a few nanometres thick.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜是仅几纳米厚的双分子层。
senses.why: The barrier is not solid but a double layer of molecules, which explains its fluid behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这层屏障并非实心，而是分子的双层，这解释了它的流动性。

senses.title: A selectively permeable barrier
senses.definition: the property of admitting some substances while excluding others
senses.definitionCN: 指允许某些物质通过、同时排斥另一些物质的性质
senses.example: The cell membrane is selectively permeable to ions.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜对离子具有选择性通透。
senses.why: The wall is picky: small neutral molecules pass, charged ones usually need help.
senses.whyCN: 这面墙很挑剔：小的中性分子能过，带电的通常需要帮助。

senses.title: The site of transport proteins
senses.definition: the place where channels, pumps and carriers move substances across
senses.definitionCN: 指通道、泵与载体把物质运送过去的地方
senses.example: Ion channels in the cell membrane open in response to a signal.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜中的离子通道会响应信号而开启。
senses.why: Because the lipid layer rejects charge, proteins must supply the doors.
senses.whyCN: 脂质层排斥电荷，因此必须由蛋白质提供门。

senses.title: A signalling interface
senses.definition: the surface where receptors detect hormones, signals or neighbouring cells
senses.definitionCN: 指受体探测激素、信号或邻近细胞的表面
senses.example: Receptors on the cell membrane detect the hormone.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜上的受体探测这种激素。
senses.why: A cell must listen before it acts, and the membrane is its ear.
senses.whyCN: 细胞要先听再行动，而细胞膜就是它的耳朵。

senses.title: A shape-giving and anchoring layer
senses.titleCN: 维持形状与锚定的结构层
senses.definition: the layer that gives the cell shape and anchors its internal skeleton and proteins
senses.definitionCN: 指赋予细胞形状、并锚定内部骨架与蛋白的层次
senses.example: The cell membrane anchors the fibres that hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜锚定维持形状的纤维。
senses.why: A thin skin can still organise everything attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 一层薄膜仍能组织起附着在它上面的一切。

senses.title: A structure compared across cell types
senses.titleCN: 不同细胞类型间的结构比较
senses.definition: the membrane as it appears in bacteria, archaea, plants or animals, with different lipids and additions
senses.definitionCN: 指细菌、古菌、植物或动物细胞中因脂质与附加结构不同而呈现的膜
senses.example: The bacterial cell membrane lacks the cholesterol found in animals.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌细胞膜缺少动物细胞中的胆固醇。
senses.why: The same barrier is built differently in different branches of life, and comparison reveals which parts are essential.
senses.whyCN: 同一道屏障在不同生命分支里造法不同，比较便能显出哪些部件必不可少。

senses.title: A model and a drug target
senses.definition: an artificial or studied membrane used to test transport, or a target for medicines
senses.definitionCN: 指用于测试运输的人工或研究对象膜，或药物作用的靶点
senses.example: Many drugs act on the cell membrane rather than inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多药物作用于细胞膜而非细胞内部。
senses.why: If the boundary is where signals arrive, it is also the easiest place to interrupt them.
senses.whyCN: 若边界是信号到达之处，它也是最容易拦截信号的地方。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room or store, and English applied it to the units of living tissue in the seventeenth century. Membrane comes from Latin membrana, a skin or parchment, generally said to derive from membrum, a limb. The compound cell membrane belongs to nineteenth-century microscopy.
intro.cn: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室、储藏间」，英语在十七世纪把它用于活组织的单位。「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」。这条合成短语属于十九世纪的显微观察传统。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 这个词意为小室、储藏间或神庙内殿。

items.en: Microscopists used the room word for the box-like spaces they saw in cork.
items.cn: 显微观察者用这个「小室」词指他们在软木中看到的格子状空间。

items.en: Membrana meant a skin, a thin covering or parchment.
items.cn: 这个词意为皮、薄膜或羊皮纸。

items.en: The word for a limb is generally taken as the base of membrana, though the link is not certain.
items.cn: 表示「肢体」的词一般认为就是「膜」这个词的基底，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: English took the Latin noun for any thin sheet, anatomical or otherwise.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，指任何薄膜，解剖学内外皆可。

items.en: Microscopists named the boundary they could see at the edge of a cell; the molecular structure was worked out in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 显微观察者为他们在细胞边缘看到的界线命名；其分子结构在二十世纪才被阐明。

note.en: The first group shares the cell or membrane element; the second group names the same barrier technically or names neighbouring structures.
note.cn: 第一组共享「细胞」或「膜」的成分；第二组是同一屏障的技术名称，或相邻结构。

entries.definition: Any thin sheet covering or lining a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖或衬在某表面的任何薄膜。

entries.definition: Made of or like a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指由膜构成的，或像膜一样的。

entries.definition: The basic unit of living tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指活组织的基本单位。

entries.definition: Relating to cells or divided into small compartments.
entries.definitionCN: 指与细胞有关的，或分成小格的。

entries.definition: The rigid outer layer of plant and bacterial cells.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物与细菌细胞外层的坚硬结构。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the membrane around a cell.
entries.definitionCN: 指包住细胞的膜的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The double molecular sheet that makes up most of the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成膜大部分的分子双层。

entries.definition: All the outer layers of a bacterium, membrane plus wall and capsule.
entries.definitionCN: 指细菌的全部外层，包括膜、壁与荚膜。

entries.definition: The lipid with a charged head that builds the bilayer.
entries.definitionCN: 指带电荷头部的脂质，构成双分子层。

entries.definition: A protein that detects a signal at the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指在膜上探测信号的蛋白质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the room and its thin wall, then the doors and ears built into that wall.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「房间」与「薄墙」展开，再想到墙上开的门与耳朵。

normal.en: A cell is a room, so its membrane is the wall.
normal.cn: 细胞是一间屋子，细胞膜就是墙。

normal.en: The wall is two layers of lipid, heads out and tails in.
normal.cn: 这面墙由两层脂质构成，头朝外、尾朝内。

normal.en: Charged ions cannot cross alone, so proteins provide doors.
normal.cn: 带电离子不能独自穿过，蛋白质便提供门。

normal.en: The membrane is also the cell's ear, full of receptors.
normal.cn: 细胞膜也是细胞的耳朵，布满受体。

normal.en: Plant cells add a wall outside the membrane; bacteria wrap both in an envelope.
normal.cn: 植物细胞在膜外再加一层壁，细菌则把两者都裹进被膜里。

abstract.en: A boundary is not a prison; it is what makes an inside possible.
abstract.cn: 边界不是监狱，而是让「内部」得以存在的东西。

abstract.en: The thinner the wall, the more carefully it must choose what passes.
abstract.cn: 墙越薄，就越要仔细选择让什么通过。

abstract.en: Every cell listens at its skin before it acts.
abstract.cn: 每个细胞都先在皮肤上倾听，然后才行动。

examples.en: The cell membrane controls the movement of salts into the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 细胞膜控制盐分进入细胞质的运动。

examples.en: Freeze-fracture reveals proteins embedded in the cell membrane.
examples.cn: 冷冻断裂法显示出嵌在细胞膜中的蛋白质。

examples.en: Some viruses fuse with the cell membrane to enter.
examples.cn: 有些病毒与细胞膜融合而进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「塞尔·门布瑞恩」——一间小室（塞尔）外面绷着一层薄膜（门布瑞恩），就是细胞膜：细胞膜、质膜

root: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室」，十七世纪被用于活组织单位；「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」，但联系不确定；合成短语属十九世纪显微观察。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses build up from the boundary itself to its molecular sheet, its selectivity, its doors, its ears, its scaffolding, its variation across cells and its use as a model or target.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从边界本身逐步往上：分子薄片、选择性、门、耳朵、支架、在不同细胞中的差异，以及作为模型或靶点的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing thin outline around a cell under a microscope, with dye stopping at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边沿停住。

branches.en: THE WALL AND ITS BUILD: the boundary, and the molecular double sheet that makes it.
branches.cn: 墙与做法：边界本身，以及构成它的分子双层。

branches.en: WHAT PASSES: selective permeability, and the proteins that open the doors.
branches.cn: 什么能过：选择性通透，以及开门的蛋白质。

branches.en: THE EAR: receptors that let a cell hear its surroundings.
branches.cn: 耳朵：让细胞听见周围环境的受体。

branches.en: THE SCAFFOLD: shape and anchoring for the cell's internal fibres.
branches.cn: 支架：为细胞内部纤维提供形状与锚定。

branches.en: THE VARIATIONS AND USES: membranes across cell types, and membranes as models or drug targets.
branches.cn: 差异与用途：不同细胞类型的膜，以及作为模型或药物靶点的膜。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin room plus a Latin skin, a plain description that later acquired a molecular meaning.
intro.cn: 这条短语是拉丁语的「房间」加「皮」，本是朴素描述，后来才获得分子层面的含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both nouns: the small room and the thin covering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供两个名词：小室与薄膜。

items.example: It is the source of cell and cellar.
items.exampleCN: 它是「细胞」与「地窖」等词的来源。

items.example: The biological sense dates from the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物学义可追溯到十七世纪。

items.example: It is the source of membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它是「膜」一词的来源。

items.example: It is generally taken as the base of the skin word, though not with certainty.
items.exampleCN: 它一般被认为是「膜」词的基底，但并不确定。

items.example: English uses it in anatomy and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 英语在解剖与化学中使用它。

items.example: It forms membranous, like a membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「膜状的」。

items.example: It gives the technical synonym plasma membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术同义词「质膜」。

items.example: It names the molecules that build the bilayer.
items.exampleCN: 它指构成双层的分子。

items.example: It forms bilayer, the two-layer structure.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「双层」。

items.example: It forms semipermeable, letting some things through.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「半透的」，即只让部分物质通过。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「皮、膜」名词构成，义为「膜」
由「膜」加形容词词尾构成，义为「膜状的」
由拉丁「小室」名词构成，义为「细胞」
由「细胞」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞的」
由次级前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚细胞的」
由表示「在内」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「细胞内的」

definition_zh: 细胞器；细胞内具有特定功能的结构
definition_en: a specialised structure inside a cell, such as a mitochondrion, chloroplast or ribosome, with a particular job
core_image: 细胞剖面图上，几个小隔间各自亮起不同颜色，像一间大屋里的小工坊
scene: 细胞剖面图上，几个小隔间各自亮起不同颜色，像一间大屋里的小工坊。Each organelle has its own job inside the cell, from energy supply to protein assembly.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（细胞器）；句意为每个细胞器在细胞内各有职责，从供能到组装蛋白质。

pos.zh: 名词：细胞器；细胞内特定功能结构

derivatives.zh: 由「细胞器」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞器的」
由「细胞器」加表示「相似」的成分构成，义为「类细胞器的」
由同一「工具、器官」词根构成，义为「器官；机构」
由「器官」加表示「相似」的词尾构成，义为「类器官」

senses.title: A specialised structure inside a cell
senses.definition: any distinct subcellular structure with a defined function
senses.definitionCN: 指细胞内任何具有明确功能的独立结构
senses.example: Every organelle in the list has a known function.
senses.exampleCN: 清单上的每个细胞器都有已知功能。
senses.why: The word was coined as a diminutive of organ, a little organ inside a cell.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「器官」的指小形式，意为细胞里的小器官。

senses.title: A membrane-bound organelle
senses.definition: an organelle enclosed by its own lipid membrane, such as a mitochondrion or a nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 指由自身脂质膜包住的细胞器，如线粒体或细胞核
senses.example: A membrane-bound organelle keeps its contents apart from the cytoplasm.
senses.exampleCN: 膜结合细胞器把自己的内容物与细胞质隔开。
senses.why: An internal membrane lets a compartment hold different chemistry from the rest of the cell.
senses.whyCN: 内部膜让一个隔间保有与细胞其余部分不同的化学环境。

senses.title: A non-membrane-bound organelle
senses.definition: a structure with a defined job but no surrounding membrane, such as a ribosome
senses.definitionCN: 指有明确功能但没有外膜的细胞结构，如核糖体
senses.example: The ribosome is a non-membrane-bound organelle.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖体是一种无膜细胞器。
senses.why: Not every organelle is a room; some are more like a machine standing in the open.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个细胞器都是房间，有些更像摆在空地上的机器。

senses.title: A named organelle with a specific role
senses.definition: a particular organelle such as a mitochondrion, chloroplast or lysosome
senses.definitionCN: 指线粒体、叶绿体或溶酶体等具体细胞器
senses.example: The mitochondrion is the organelle that releases energy from food.
senses.exampleCN: 线粒体是从食物中释放能量的细胞器。
senses.why: Once each structure was separated, it could be named and assigned a task.
senses.whyCN: 各结构被分离出来之后，便可逐一命名并分派任务。

senses.title: An organelle genome
senses.definition: the small set of genes carried inside an organelle such as a mitochondrion or chloroplast
senses.definitionCN: 指线粒体或叶绿体等细胞器内部携带的一小组基因
senses.example: The chloroplast organelle still carries its own DNA.
senses.exampleCN: 叶绿体细胞器仍携带自己的遗传物质。
senses.why: Some organelles keep a remnant genome, evidence of their independent ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 有些细胞器保留残余基因组，这是它们曾独立起源的证据。

senses.title: An organelle in a single-celled organism
senses.titleCN: 单细胞生物中的细胞器
senses.definition: the equivalent structures in bacteria, protists and other unicellular life
senses.definitionCN: 指细菌、原生生物等单细胞生命中的对应结构
senses.example: A protist may use a contractile organelle to expel water.
senses.exampleCN: 原生生物可能用一种可收缩的细胞器排出水分。
senses.why: Single cells do inside one body what tissues do across many.
senses.whyCN: 单细胞在一个身体里完成组织在许多细胞间完成的事。

senses.title: The older sense of a small organ
senses.definition: in older anatomical writing, a small organ or an organ-like part
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的解剖学文献中，指小器官或类似器官的部分
senses.example: Early texts called the structure a little organelle of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 早期文献把这个结构称作身体的小器官。
senses.why: The diminutive began in anatomy and was later borrowed by cell biology.
senses.whyCN: 这个指小词最初用于解剖学，后来被细胞生物学借用。

senses.title: An engineered or diseased organelle
senses.titleCN: 被改造或发生病变的细胞器
senses.definition: an organelle modified in the laboratory or one whose failure causes disease
senses.definitionCN: 指在实验室中被改造的细胞器，或因功能失常而致病的细胞器
senses.example: A synthetic organelle can be built to store a new product.
senses.exampleCN: 可以构建一种合成细胞器来储存新产物。
senses.why: Understanding the part lets researchers repair it or replace its job.
senses.whyCN: 了解这个部件之后，研究者便能修理它或替换它的职能。

intro.en: Organelle is a diminutive of organ: Greek organon, a tool or instrument, became Latin organum and English organ, and the French diminutive ending -elle made a little organ. Cell biologists adopted it in the nineteenth century for the small bodies they saw inside cells.
intro.cn: 这个词是「器官」的指小形式：希腊语 organon「工具、器具」变成拉丁语 organum 与英语 organ，再加法语指小词尾，成为「小器官」。细胞生物学家在十九世纪用它指他们在细胞内看到的小体。

items.en: Organon meant a tool, an instrument or an organ of the body.
items.cn: 这个词意为工具、器具或身体器官。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for an instrument or an organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊词，指器具或器官。

items.en: English used it for body parts, for musical instruments and for organized bodies.
items.cn: 英语用它指身体部位、乐器与有组织的机构。

items.en: The diminutive ending made a small version of a noun.
items.cn: 这个指小词尾构成名词的「小」版本。

items.en: Cell biologists used the little-organ word for the bodies visible inside cells; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
items.cn: 细胞生物学家用「小器官」这个词指细胞内可见的小体；确切造词年份不确定。

items.en: Electron microscopy and cell fractionation turned the word into a classified family of structures.
items.cn: 电子显微镜与细胞分级分离把这个词变成一组被分类的结构。

note.en: The first group shares the organ root or the diminutive ending; the second group names particular organelles and related structures.
note.cn: 第一组共享「器官」词根或指小词尾；第二组是具体细胞器与相关结构。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有特定功能的器官，或指乐器。

entries.definition: A lab-grown miniature organ-like structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指实验室培养的微型类器官结构。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of or belonging to organelles.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于细胞器的形容词。

entries.definition: Resembling an organelle in structure or function.
entries.definitionCN: 指在结构或功能上像细胞器。

entries.definition: Relating to living things or to carbon chemistry, from the same instrument word.
entries.definitionCN: 指与生物或碳化学有关的，同出「器官」词根。

entries.definition: The organelle that produces most of the cell's energy.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生细胞大部分能量的细胞器。

entries.definition: The plant organelle where photosynthesis happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物细胞中进行光合作用的细胞器。

entries.definition: The non-membrane-bound organelle that assembles proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 指组装蛋白质的无膜细胞器。

entries.definition: A membrane-bound compartment for storage or waste.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于储存或处理废物的膜结合隔间。

entries.definition: A body inside a cell that is not usually called an organelle.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞内通常不称为细胞器的小体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the little organ: a workshop inside a room.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「小器官」展开：房间里的一个个小工坊。

normal.en: Organ plus a diminutive ending: a little organ inside a cell.
normal.cn: 器官加指小词尾：细胞里的小器官。

normal.en: Membrane-bound organelles are rooms; ribosomes are machines in the open.
normal.cn: 膜结合细胞器是房间，核糖体是摆在空地上的机器。

normal.en: The mitochondrion releases energy, the chloroplast captures it.
normal.cn: 线粒体释放能量，叶绿体捕获能量。

normal.en: Some organelles keep their own DNA, a trace of independent ancestry.
normal.cn: 有些细胞器保留自己的遗传物质，是独立起源的痕迹。

normal.en: A synthetic organelle is a new workshop built on purpose.
normal.cn: 合成细胞器是特意新建的工坊。

abstract.en: Division of labour works at every scale, down to a single cell.
abstract.cn: 分工在每一个尺度上都成立，直到单个细胞之内。

abstract.en: A compartment is a promise that two chemistries will not mix.
abstract.cn: 隔间是一个承诺：两种化学环境不会混在一起。

abstract.en: Knowing what a part does is the first step to repairing it.
abstract.cn: 知道一个部件做什么，是修理它的第一步。

examples.en: The organelle was first described under an electron microscope.
examples.cn: 这个细胞器最早是在电子显微镜下被描述的。

examples.en: Each organelle carries a marker that identifies its type.
examples.cn: 每个细胞器都带有识别其类型的标记。

examples.en: Loss of the organelle stops the cell from storing starch.
examples.cn: 该细胞器的丧失使细胞无法储存淀粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥格内尔」——器官（奥格）缩小成「内尔」小间，就是细胞器：细胞器、小器官

root: 希腊语 organon「工具、器官」经拉丁语 organum 与英语 organ，再加法语指小词尾构成「小器官」；十九世纪被细胞生物学用来指细胞内小体，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from any specialised cell structure to the membrane-bound and open kinds, named examples, their genomes, single-cell versions, the older anatomical sense and engineered or diseased forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从任何专职细胞结构出发，走向有膜与无膜两类、具体例子、它们的基因组、单细胞版本、较早的解剖义，以及被改造或病变的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut-away cell with several small coloured workshops, each doing a different job.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞剖面图上几个亮着不同颜色的小工坊，各自干不同的活。

branches.en: THE NAME: any specialised body, and the older anatomical sense of a little organ.
branches.cn: 名称：任何专职小体，以及较早的解剖学「小器官」义。

branches.en: THE TWO KINDS: rooms with membranes, and machines without them.
branches.cn: 两类形态：有膜的隔间，与无膜的机器。

branches.en: THE WORKERS: named organelles with known jobs, also found in single cells.
branches.cn: 工作者：有已知职责的具名细胞器，也见于单细胞生物。

branches.en: THE INHERITANCE: a small genome kept inside the organelle.
branches.cn: 遗传：细胞器内部保留的一小组基因。

branches.en: THE MADE AND THE BROKEN: engineered organelles and organelles whose failure causes disease.
branches.cn: 被造与被损：工程化细胞器，以及功能失常致病的细胞器。

intro.en: The word is one Greek noun for a tool, one Latin borrowing, one English shortening and one French diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个希腊「工具」名词、一个拉丁借词、一个英语缩短形式与一个法语指小词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word for instrument; the diminutive ending reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语表示「器具」的词；指小词尾经法语进入英语。

items.example: It is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整族词的来源。

items.example: Latin passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把它传给英语。

items.example: English uses it for both flesh and music.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它指身体部位，也指乐器。

items.example: It turns organ into a little organ.
items.exampleCN: 它把「器官」变成「小器官」。

items.example: Cell biology gave the little organ its modern meaning.
items.exampleCN: 细胞生物学赋予「小器官」现代含义。

items.example: It forms organellar, belonging to organelles.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「细胞器的」。

items.example: It forms organoid, a structure resembling an organ.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「类器官」。

items.example: It forms organic from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它由同一词根构成「有机的」。

derivatives.zh: 由「细胞器」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞器的」
由「细胞器」加「相似」成分构成，义为「类细胞器的」
由拉丁「器具、器官」名词构成，义为「器官」
由「器官」加「相似」词尾构成，义为「类器官」

definition_zh: 脱氧核糖核酸；遗传物质；遗传信息的载体
definition_en: deoxyribonucleic acid, the long double-stranded molecule that stores the inherited instructions of living cells
core_image: 实验室里一条双螺旋模型在灯下旋转，彩色条带一段段咬合
scene: 实验室里一条双螺旋模型在灯下旋转，彩色条带一段段咬合。DNA carries the instructions that cells use to build and copy themselves.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（脱氧核糖核酸分子）；句意为脱氧核糖核酸携带细胞用来建造与复制自身的指令。

pos.zh: 名词缩写：脱氧核糖核酸；遗传物质；遗传信息载体

collocations.zh: 脱氧核糖核酸指纹分析

derivatives.zh: 由缩写加表示「酶」的词尾构成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸酶」
由缩写与「以……为基础」成分复合而成，义为「基于脱氧核糖核酸的」
由缩写与「结合」成分复合而成，义为「结合脱氧核糖核酸的」
由「线粒体的」与缩写复合而成，义为「线粒体脱氧核糖核酸」
由「重组的」与缩写复合而成，义为「重组脱氧核糖核酸」
由缩写与「指纹分析」复合而成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸指纹分析」

senses.title: The double-stranded molecule
senses.definition: the long molecule made of two paired strands wound into a double helix
senses.definitionCN: 指由两条配对链缠绕成双螺旋的长分子
senses.example: DNA is a double helix held together by paired bases.
senses.exampleCN: 脱氧核糖核酸是双螺旋，由配对碱基维系。
senses.why: The abbreviation names a chemical, and its shape is the first thing anyone learns about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩写指一种化学物质，而它的形状是任何人最先学到的东西。

senses.title: The material of inheritance
senses.definition: the substance that passes genetic information from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指把遗传信息由亲代传给子代的物质
senses.example: DNA transmits traits from one generation to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 脱氧核糖核酸把性状从一代传到下一代。
senses.why: Once it was shown to carry genes, the molecule became the physical basis of heredity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦证明它携带基因，这个分子就成了遗传的物理基础。

senses.title: A sequence or genetic code
senses.definition: the ordered string of bases that spells out a gene or a whole genome
senses.definitionCN: 指拼出一个基因或整个基因组的碱基顺序
senses.example: The DNA of this species has been sequenced.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的脱氧核糖核酸已被测序。
senses.why: The molecule is also a text, and the word often means the message rather than the paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子也是一段文本，因此这个词常指信息而非载体。

senses.title: A sample or a test
senses.definition: material taken for identification, as in forensic or paternity testing
senses.definitionCN: 指用于身份识别而采集的材料，如法医或亲子鉴定
senses.example: The lab compared DNA from the two samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室比对了两个样本中的脱氧核糖核酸。
senses.why: A test turns the abstract molecule into evidence that can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 检测把这个抽象分子变成可供比对的证据。

senses.title: The essential character of something
senses.definition: the core pattern that makes an organization, style or idea what it is
senses.definitionCN: 指使一个组织、风格或想法成其为自身的核心模式
senses.example: Innovation is in the DNA of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 创新已写在这家公司的根本特质里。
senses.why: The code image invites metaphor: whatever is copied faithfully becomes a genetic text.
senses.whyCN: 密码的意象引出比喻：凡被忠实复制的东西都可说成一段遗传文本。

senses.title: Engineered or recombinant DNA
senses.titleCN: 被工程改造的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.definition: DNA cut and rejoined in the laboratory to combine sequences from different sources
senses.definitionCN: 指在实验室中被切割并重新连接、以组合不同来源序列的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.example: Recombinant DNA made human insulin possible.
senses.exampleCN: 重组脱氧核糖核酸使生产人胰岛素成为可能。
senses.why: Once the molecule could be cut and pasted, it became a construction material.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子一旦能被剪切与拼接，就成了一种建筑材料。

senses.title: DNA as a storage medium
senses.titleCN: 作为存储介质的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.definition: the use of synthetic DNA to encode digital data at very high density
senses.definitionCN: 指用合成脱氧核糖核酸以极高密度编码数字数据
senses.example: Researchers wrote a film into DNA and read it back.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把一部影片写入脱氧核糖核酸，再读回来。
senses.why: The same property that makes it a good archive, stability, makes it slow to read.
senses.whyCN: 使它成为优良档案的稳定性，也使它读取缓慢。

senses.title: The spelled-out chemical name
senses.definition: the full name deoxyribonucleic acid, used when the abbreviation needs defining
senses.definitionCN: 指在需要解释缩写时使用的全称「脱氧核糖核酸」
senses.example: The report defines DNA in its first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在第一段就给出脱氧核糖核酸的全称。
senses.why: An abbreviation is only useful if it is unpacked once, and dictionaries do that work.
senses.whyCN: 缩写只有被展开一次才有用，词典承担这项工作。

intro.en: DNA is an abbreviation, not a root. It shortens deoxyribonucleic acid: nucleic from Latin nucleus, a kernel or the core of a cell; ribo from ribose, the sugar in the chain; deoxy marking the loss of one oxygen atom; acid from Latin acidus, sour. The abbreviation became standard in the mid-twentieth century, and its exact first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这是一个缩写而非词根。它缩短了「脱氧核糖核酸」这一全称：其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，指细胞核；「核糖」指链中的糖；「脱氧」标记少了一个氧原子；「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」。这个缩写在二十世纪中期成为通用写法，确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: Nucleus meant a kernel or a nut, and it gave the name to the cell's core.
items.cn: 这个词意为果核、坚果，后来用来命名细胞核。

items.en: Chemists found an acid rich in phosphorus inside cell nuclei and named it after the nucleus.
items.cn: 化学家在细胞核内发现一种富含磷的酸，便按「核」给它命名。

items.en: The five-carbon sugar in the chain gave the element ribo-.
items.cn: 链中的五碳糖提供了「核糖」这一成分。

items.en: The prefix marks the removal of one oxygen atom from the sugar, a difference from RNA.
items.cn: 这一前缀标记糖上少了一个氧原子，这正是与核糖核酸的区别。

items.en: The initials replaced the full chemical name as knowledge of heredity grew; the precise first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着遗传知识的发展，首字母缩写取代了化学全称；确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: The published structure gave the abbreviation a shape that could be drawn, taught and remembered.
items.cn: 结构的发表使这个缩写有了可绘制、可教学、可记忆的形状。

note.en: The first group shares the abbreviation or the chemical family; the second group names the things DNA is confused with or the units it contains.
note.cn: 第一组共享这一缩写或同一化学家族；第二组是容易与它混淆的概念，以及它所包含的单位。

entries.definition: Ribonucleic acid, which carries and translates instructions rather than storing them long-term.
entries.definitionCN: 核糖核酸，负责传递与翻译指令，而非长期储存。

entries.definition: Complementary DNA copied from an RNA template.
entries.definitionCN: 指以核糖核酸为模板复制出的互补脱氧核糖核酸。

entries.definition: The small DNA genome inside mitochondria, inherited from the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指线粒体内的小型基因组，由母方遗传。

entries.definition: An enzyme that cuts DNA strands.
entries.definitionCN: 指切割脱氧核糖核酸链的酶。

entries.definition: The single unit, base plus sugar plus phosphate, that builds the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成链的单个单位，即碱基加糖加磷酸。

entries.definition: A stretch of DNA that codes for a product or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指编码一种产物或一个性状的一段脱氧核糖核酸。

entries.definition: The complete set of genetic material in an organism.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个生物体的全部遗传物质。

entries.definition: The packaged structure in which DNA is carried.
entries.definitionCN: 指承载脱氧核糖核酸的包装结构。

entries.definition: The chemical family to which DNA and RNA belong.
entries.definitionCN: 指脱氧核糖核酸与核糖核酸所属的化学家族。

entries.definition: The twisted two-strand shape of the molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指该分子两条链缠绕的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations unpack the initials: sugar, nucleus, acid, and the paired strands.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把首字母展开：糖、核、酸，以及配对的链。

normal.en: The D means one oxygen has been removed from the sugar.
normal.cn: 开头的字母表示糖上少了一个氧原子。

normal.en: The N points to the nucleus, where the acid was first found.
normal.cn: 中间的字母指向细胞核，那种酸最早在那里被发现。

normal.en: The A is acid, from the Latin word for sour.
normal.cn: 末尾的字母是「酸」，出自拉丁语表示「酸」的词。

normal.en: Two strands pair their bases and twist into a double helix.
normal.cn: 两条链让碱基配对，再缠成双螺旋。

normal.en: Recombinant DNA is cut and pasted, like text in an editor.
normal.cn: 重组脱氧核糖核酸被剪切拼接，就像在编辑器里改文本。

abstract.en: An abbreviation is a promise that everyone already knows the long name.
abstract.cn: 缩写是一个约定：大家都已知道那个全称。

abstract.en: A molecule that copies itself is also a message that outlives its sender.
abstract.cn: 一个能自我复制的分子，也是一条比发送者活得更久的讯息。

abstract.en: Saying something is in the DNA means it will be copied whether you like it or not.
abstract.cn: 说某事物「写在基因里」，意思是它不管你喜欢与否都会被复制。

examples.en: DNA was extracted from the bone and compared with a reference sample.
examples.cn: 从骨骼中提取脱氧核糖核酸，并与参考样本比对。

examples.en: Errors copied into DNA can be repaired by the cell's own enzymes.
examples.cn: 复制进脱氧核糖核酸的错误可由细胞自身的酶修复。

examples.en: The company treats careful testing as part of its DNA.
examples.cn: 这家公司把谨慎测试视为自身根本特质的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「地恩埃」——三个字母像双螺旋的三段台阶，记住全称「脱氧核糖核酸」即可

root: 这是缩写，并非词根：全称由「脱氧」「核糖」「核酸」组合，其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」；缩写于二十世纪中期通用，确切首见时间不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from the molecule and its hereditary role to its sequence, its sample, its metaphorical use, its engineered form, its archival use and its spelled-out name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从分子本身与遗传作用出发，走向序列、样本、比喻用法、工程形式、存档用途，以及展开的全称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit double helix on a lab bench, coloured rungs pairing one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：实验台上被灯照亮的双螺旋，彩色横档一节节配对。

branches.en: THE NAME AND THE SHAPE: the molecule, and the full chemical name behind the initials.
branches.cn: 名称与形状：分子本身，以及首字母背后的化学全称。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: the material of inheritance, and the base sequence that spells it.
branches.cn: 信息：遗传物质，以及拼出信息的碱基序列。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: a sample taken and compared.
branches.cn: 证据：被采集并比对的样本。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: the copied core of an organization or style.
branches.cn: 比喻：一个组织或风格中被复制的核心。

branches.en: THE TOOL: DNA cut and rejoined, and DNA used as a dense archive.
branches.cn: 工具：被剪切重接的脱氧核糖核酸，以及被当作高密度档案的脱氧核糖核酸。

intro.en: The word is an abbreviation, so its parts are the parts of the full chemical name rather than old roots.
intro.cn: 这是一个缩写，因此它的部件是全称中的化学部件，而不是古老词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the nucleus and the acid; the sugar and the oxygen prefix belong to modern chemical naming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了「核」与「酸」，糖与「脱氧」前缀则属于现代化学命名。

items.example: It gives nucleic, the acid of the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「核酸」，即细胞核中的酸。

items.example: It forms nucleic from nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它由「核」构成「核酸的」。

items.example: It gives acid, the final word of the full name.
items.exampleCN: 它构成全称末尾的「酸」。

items.example: It gives the ribo- element.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「核糖」这一成分。

items.example: It marks the difference from the RNA sugar.
items.exampleCN: 它标记与核糖核酸所用糖的差别。

items.example: The initials are read letter by letter.
items.exampleCN: 这三个字母逐字母读出。

items.example: It forms DNase, an enzyme that cuts DNA.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「脱氧核糖核酸酶」。

items.example: It names the twisted shape of the two strands.
items.exampleCN: 它指两条链缠绕的形状。

derivatives.zh: 由缩写加酶名词尾构成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸酶」
由缩写加「以……为基础」成分构成，义为「基于脱氧核糖核酸的」
由缩写加「结合」成分构成，义为「结合脱氧核糖核酸的」
由「线粒体的」与缩写复合而成，义为「线粒体脱氧核糖核酸」
由「重组的」与缩写复合而成，义为「重组脱氧核糖核酸」
由缩写与「指纹分析」复合而成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸指纹分析」

definition_zh: 核糖核酸；传递遗传信息的核酸；核糖核酸类分子
definition_en: ribonucleic acid, a single-stranded nucleic acid that carries, translates or regulates genetic instructions
core_image: 实验室里一段单链从模板上被抄下，随后离开核区去组装蛋白
scene: 实验室里一段单链从模板上被抄下，随后离开核区去组装蛋白。RNA copies a stretch of DNA and carries that message out of the nucleus.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（核糖核酸分子）；句意为核糖核酸抄下一段脱氧核糖核酸，并把这条信息带出细胞核。

pos.zh: 名词缩写：核糖核酸；遗传信息的传递与调控分子

derivatives.zh: 由缩写加表示「酶」的词尾构成，义为「核糖核酸酶」
由表示「信使」的成分与缩写复合而成，义为「信使核糖核酸」

由缩写与「以……为基础」成分复合而成，义为「基于核糖核酸的」
由缩写与「结合」成分复合而成，义为「结合核糖核酸的」
由缩写与表示「干扰」的成分复合而成，义为「核糖核酸干扰」

senses.title: The single-stranded molecule
senses.definition: the nucleic acid built from ribose, phosphate and bases, usually single-stranded
senses.definitionCN: 指由核糖、磷酸与碱基构成、通常为单链的核酸
senses.example: RNA is usually single-stranded, unlike DNA.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖核酸通常是单链，与脱氧核糖核酸不同。
senses.why: The extra oxygen in its sugar is the only chemical difference, but it changes the molecule's behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 其糖上多出的一个氧原子是唯一的化学差别，却改变了分子的行为。

senses.title: Messenger RNA
senses.definition: the transcript copied from a gene and read by the ribosome
senses.definitionCN: 指从基因抄下、由核糖体阅读的转录本
senses.example: Messenger RNA carries the recipe from the gene to the ribosome.
senses.exampleCN: 信使核糖核酸把配方从基因送到核糖体。
senses.why: The molecule's main everyday role is to move a message, not to keep it.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子日常的主要角色是搬运信息，而不是保存信息。

senses.title: The machinery of translation
senses.titleCN: 翻译机器中的核糖核酸
senses.definition: ribosomal and transfer RNA that build proteins from the message
senses.definitionCN: 指按信息建造蛋白质的核糖体核糖核酸与转运核糖核酸
senses.example: Transfer RNA brings the matching amino acid to the ribosome.
senses.exampleCN: 转运核糖核酸把对应的氨基酸送到核糖体。
senses.why: Some RNA is not a message but a tool, part of the factory itself.
senses.whyCN: 有些核糖核酸不是信息，而是工具，是工厂本身的一部分。

senses.title: A viral genome
senses.definition: the genetic material of viruses that store their instructions as RNA
senses.definitionCN: 指以核糖核酸储存遗传指令的病毒所带的遗传物质
senses.example: The influenza virus stores its genome as RNA.
senses.exampleCN: 流感病毒以核糖核酸储存基因组。
senses.why: Viruses show that DNA is not the only possible archive.
senses.whyCN: 病毒说明脱氧核糖核酸并非唯一可能的档案。

senses.title: The RNA world hypothesis
senses.definition: the proposed early stage of life in which RNA both stored information and catalysed reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指生命早期阶段的一种假说，认为核糖核酸同时储存信息并催化反应
senses.example: The RNA world idea explains how catalysis and inheritance could start together.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖核酸世界的想法解释了催化与遗传如何同时起步。
senses.why: One molecule doing two jobs is simpler than two molecules doing one each.
senses.whyCN: 一个分子兼两职，比两个分子各司一职更简单。

senses.title: RNA interference and regulation
senses.definition: small RNAs that switch genes off or adjust how much product is made
senses.definitionCN: 指关闭基因或调节产物数量的小型核糖核酸
senses.example: RNA interference can silence a gene without changing its sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖核酸干扰能在不改变序列的情况下关闭一个基因。
senses.why: The molecule is also a control signal, not merely a courier.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子也是控制信号，而不只是信差。

senses.title: RNA vaccines and therapeutics
senses.definition: medical products that deliver an RNA message so the body makes a protein itself
senses.definitionCN: 指递送核糖核酸信息、让身体自行制造蛋白质的医疗产品
senses.example: The RNA vaccine instructs cells to make a harmless viral protein.
senses.exampleCN: 核糖核酸疫苗指示细胞制造一种无害的病毒蛋白。
senses.why: If the body can read the message, the message can be the medicine.
senses.whyCN: 只要身体能读这条信息，信息本身就可以成为药物。

senses.title: The spelled-out chemical name
senses.definition: the full name ribonucleic acid, used when the abbreviation is defined
senses.definitionCN: 指解释缩写时使用的全称「核糖核酸」
senses.example: The glossary expands RNA on first use.
senses.exampleCN: 术语表在首次出现时展开核糖核酸的全称。
senses.why: Abbreviations need one clear expansion before they can travel.
senses.whyCN: 缩写需要先有一次清楚展开，才能通行。

intro.en: RNA abbreviates ribonucleic acid. Nucleic comes from Latin nucleus, a kernel; ribo refers to ribose, the sugar in the chain; acid comes from Latin acidus, sour. The initials became standard in the mid-twentieth century, and the exact first use is uncertain. The molecule differs from DNA by one oxygen atom in its sugar.
intro.cn: 这个缩写展开为「核糖核酸」：其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，「核糖」指链中的糖，「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」。首字母缩写在二十世纪中期成为通用写法，确切首见时间不确定。它与脱氧核糖核酸的差别在于糖上少了一个氧原子。

items.en: Nucleus meant a kernel, and the acid of the cell nucleus took its name.
items.cn: 这个词意为果核，细胞核中的那种酸便由此得名。

items.en: The phosphorus-rich acid isolated from cell nuclei was named after the nucleus.
items.cn: 从细胞核中分离出的富磷酸被按「核」命名。

items.en: The five-carbon sugar in the chain supplied the ribo- element.
items.cn: 链中的五碳糖提供了「核糖」这一成分。

items.en: The initials replaced the full chemical name as the molecule's roles became clear; the precise first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着分子的各种作用逐渐清楚，首字母缩写取代了化学全称；确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: The discovery of a short-lived transcript gave RNA a verb-like role: carrying a message.
items.cn: 短寿命转录本的发现赋予核糖核酸一个动词式的角色：传递信息。

items.en: The hypothesis that early life relied on RNA was named in the later twentieth century; the exact naming date is uncertain.
items.cn: 早期生命依赖核糖核酸的假说在二十世纪后期得名，确切命名年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the abbreviation shape; the second group names its types and the things it interacts with.
note.cn: 第一组共享缩写形式；第二组是它的类型与相互作用的对象。

entries.definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid, the double-stranded archive of inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 脱氧核糖核酸，双链的遗传档案。

entries.definition: Messenger RNA, the transcript read by ribosomes.
entries.definitionCN: 信使核糖核酸，被核糖体阅读的转录本。

entries.definition: Ribosomal RNA, part of the protein-building factory.
entries.definitionCN: 核糖体核糖核酸，蛋白质工厂的组成部分。

entries.definition: Transfer RNA, which brings amino acids into place.
entries.definitionCN: 转运核糖核酸，把氨基酸送到位置。

entries.definition: An enzyme that breaks RNA down.
entries.definitionCN: 指分解核糖核酸的酶。

entries.definition: The RNA copy made from a gene.
entries.definitionCN: 指从基因抄出的核糖核酸副本。

entries.definition: The chemical family that includes both DNA and RNA.
entries.definitionCN: 指包括脱氧核糖核酸与核糖核酸的化学家族。

entries.definition: The particle that reads mRNA and builds protein.
entries.definitionCN: 指阅读信使核糖核酸并建造蛋白质的颗粒。

entries.definition: A three-base group that specifies one amino acid.
entries.definitionCN: 指规定一个氨基酸的三个碱基组合。

entries.definition: A particle that may carry its instructions as RNA.
entries.definitionCN: 指可能以核糖核酸携带遗传指令的颗粒。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations unpack the initials and the jobs the molecule does.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把首字母展开，并记住这个分子承担的几项工作。

normal.en: Ribose plus nucleic plus acid: the sugar is the one with its oxygen kept.
normal.cn: 核糖加核酸加酸：这种糖保留着那个氧原子。

normal.en: DNA stores, RNA carries; the courier leaves the nucleus.
normal.cn: 脱氧核糖核酸储存，核糖核酸搬运；信差离开细胞核。

normal.en: mRNA is the message, tRNA the delivery, rRNA the factory floor.
normal.cn: 信使是信息，转运是送货，核糖体是车间地面。

normal.en: Some viruses keep their whole genome as RNA.
normal.cn: 有些病毒把整个基因组存成核糖核酸。

normal.en: An RNA vaccine gives the body a message instead of a product.
normal.cn: 核糖核酸疫苗给身体的是信息，而不是成品。

abstract.en: Storing and doing need not be separate jobs; early life may have used one molecule for both.
abstract.cn: 储存与执行不必分开，早期生命也许用一个分子兼做两事。

abstract.en: A message that can silence a gene is also a form of control.
abstract.cn: 能关闭基因的信息，也是一种控制方式。

abstract.en: The shortest-lived copy can be the most important one.
abstract.cn: 寿命最短的副本，可能是最重要的那一份。

examples.en: RNA is copied from DNA in a process called transcription.
examples.cn: 核糖核酸在称为转录的过程中从脱氧核糖核酸抄下。

examples.en: Some RNA molecules fold into shapes that catalyse reactions.
examples.cn: 有些核糖核酸分子折叠成能催化反应的形状。

examples.en: The test detects viral RNA in a sample.
examples.cn: 这项检测在样本中寻找病毒核糖核酸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿尔恩埃」——比脱氧核糖核酸少一个氧，单链的「信差」：核糖核酸、传递遗传信息

root: 这是缩写，并非词根：全称由「核糖」「核酸」组合，其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」；缩写于二十世纪中期通用，确切首见时间不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the molecule from its chemistry to its messenger and machine roles, its viral use, its early-life hypothesis, its regulatory and medical uses, and its spelled-out name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从化学分子出发，依次走向信使与机器角色、病毒用途、早期生命假说、调控与医疗用途，以及展开的全称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single strand copied from a template, leaving the nucleus to build a protein.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段单链从模板上被抄下，离开细胞核去建造蛋白质。

branches.en: THE NAME AND THE MOLECULE: the single strand, and the chemical name behind the initials.
branches.cn: 名称与分子：单链本身，以及首字母背后的化学全称。

branches.en: THE COURIER: a transcript carrying a gene's recipe.
branches.cn: 信差：携带基因配方的转录本。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE VIRUS: RNA that builds protein, and viral genomes kept as RNA.
branches.cn: 机器与病毒：建造蛋白质的核糖核酸，以及以核糖核酸储存的病毒基因组。

branches.en: THE EARLY WORLD: a molecule that could both store and catalyse.
branches.cn: 早期世界：既能储存又能催化的分子。

branches.en: THE SWITCH AND THE DRUG: regulatory RNA, and RNA delivered as medicine.
branches.cn: 开关与药物：调控性核糖核酸，以及作为药物递送的核糖核酸。

intro.en: Like DNA, this word is an abbreviation whose parts come from chemistry rather than from old roots.
intro.cn: 与脱氧核糖核酸一样，这个词也是缩写，其部件来自化学命名而非古老词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the nucleus and the acid; the sugar and the initials belong to modern chemistry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「核」与「酸」；糖与首字母属于现代化学。

items.example: It gives nucleic, the acid of the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「核酸」。

items.example: It forms nucleic from nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它由「核」构成「核酸的」。

items.example: It gives the final word of the full name.
items.exampleCN: 它构成全称末尾的「酸」。

items.example: It supplies the ribo- element.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「核糖」成分。

items.example: The initials are read letter by letter.
items.exampleCN: 这三个字母逐字母读出。

items.example: It forms RNase, an enzyme that cuts RNA.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「核糖核酸酶」。

items.example: It forms mRNA, the transcript.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「信使核糖核酸」。

items.example: It forms RNAi, the silencing pathway.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「核糖核酸干扰」。

由「信使」成分与缩写复合而成，义为「信使核糖核酸」

由缩写加「干扰」成分构成，义为「核糖核酸干扰」

definition_zh: 幸存；生存；存活；残存物；（物种或机构的）延续
definition_en: the state of continuing to live or exist through danger, difficulty or time, or a thing that has outlasted its setting
core_image: 暴风雪中一间小屋的窗透出微光，炉边的人裹着毯子等天亮
scene: 暴风雪中一间小屋的窗透出微光，炉边的人裹着毯子等天亮。Survival through the night depended on a fire and dry blankets.
sceneCN: 这里取第 2 个义项（在危险中活下来）；句意为熬过这一夜靠的是一炉火与干燥的毯子。

pos.zh: 名词：幸存；生存；存活率；残存物；延续

collocations.phrase: a survival from an earlier age
collocations.zh: 来自较早时代的残存物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「在……之上活着」经法语进入英语，义为「活下来；比……活得久」
由动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「幸存者」
由动词加表示「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可幸存的」
由形容词加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「可存活程度」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「仍然存活的；残存的」
由「生存」加表示主张者的词尾构成，义为「生存主义者」

senses.title: Continuing to live
senses.definition: the state of remaining alive from one moment to the next
senses.definitionCN: 指从一个时刻到下一个时刻持续活着的状态
senses.example: Clean water is the first condition of survival.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁的水是生存的第一条件。
senses.why: The noun simply names the state behind the verb: to keep living.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词就是动词背后的状态：持续活着。

senses.title: Coming through a dangerous event
senses.definition: the act of living through a hazard such as a storm, a fire or an illness
senses.definitionCN: 指经历风暴、火灾或疾病等危险而活下来
senses.example: Survival through the night depended on a fire and dry blankets.
senses.exampleCN: 熬过这一夜靠的是一炉火与干燥的毯子。
senses.why: The word usually implies a threat that could have ended the story.
senses.whyCN: 这个词通常暗含一个本可终结故事的威胁。

senses.title: Outliving another person
senses.definition: continuing to live after another person has died
senses.definitionCN: 指在另一人去世之后仍继续活着
senses.example: Her survival of her brother left her the last of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她比哥哥活得久，成了家里最后一人。
senses.why: The older sense is comparative: survival is measured against someone else's death.
senses.whyCN: 较早的义项是比较性的：存活是相对他人的死亡来衡量的。

senses.title: A thing left from an earlier age
senses.definition: a custom, object or word that persists after the conditions that produced it have gone
senses.definitionCN: 指产生它的条件消失之后仍留存的习俗、物件或词语
senses.example: The ceremony is a survival from the days of open-field farming.
senses.exampleCN: 这一仪式是敞开田耕作时代的残存物。
senses.why: Culture, like biology, keeps traces that no longer serve their original purpose.
senses.whyCN: 文化与生物一样，会保留已不再服务于原初目的的痕迹。

senses.title: A survival rate in statistics
senses.definition: the proportion of a group still alive after a stated period or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指一组个体在经过某段时间或某种治疗之后仍存活的比例
senses.example: The five-year survival rate has improved steadily.
senses.exampleCN: 五年存活率一直在稳步提高。
senses.why: Counting survivors turns a story into a number that medicine can compare.
senses.whyCN: 清点幸存者把故事变成一个医学可以比较的数字。

senses.title: Differential survival in evolution
senses.definition: the unequal chance that individuals of different traits leave offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指具有不同性状的个体留下后代的几率不相等
senses.example: Natural selection works through differences in survival.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择通过存活差异起作用。
senses.why: Evolution needs only that some variants live longer enough to reproduce more.
senses.whyCN: 演化只要求某些变体活得稍久、从而繁殖更多。

senses.title: Survival as an attributive skill set
senses.definition: used before another noun for the skills, equipment or training needed to stay alive
senses.definitionCN: 用于另一名词之前，指维持生命所需的技能、装备或训练
senses.example: The course teaches survival skills in cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程教授冷水中的生存技能。
senses.why: The noun turns into an adjective of preparation, common in training and marketing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词转为表示准备的定语，常见于训练与市场语境。

senses.title: The continuance of an organization
senses.definition: the continued existence of a company, institution or project under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 指公司、机构或项目在压力下继续存在
senses.example: The firm's survival depends on cutting fixed costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的存续取决于削减固定成本。
senses.why: Organizations borrow the biological word because both must keep going or disappear.
senses.whyCN: 机构借用生物学的词，因为两者都必须继续存在，否则消失。

senses.title: The continuation of a species
senses.definition: the persistence of a population or lineage over generations
senses.definitionCN: 指一个种群或世系在世代之间持续存在
senses.example: The survival of the species may depend on a single wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的延续可能取决于一片湿地。
senses.why: At the largest scale, survival is about lineages rather than individuals.
senses.whyCN: 在最大尺度上，存续关乎世系而非个体。

senses.title: A relic kept by habit
senses.definition: in linguistics and folklore, a form that survives outside its original system
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学与民俗学中，指在原系统之外仍存留的形式
senses.example: The word is a survival in modern dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词是现代方言中的遗留形式。
senses.why: Language keeps old forms in corners long after the grammar that produced them has changed.
senses.whyCN: 语言会把旧形式留在角落里，即使产生它的语法早已改变。

intro.en: Survival comes from survive, which entered English through Anglo-French from Latin supervivere, to live beyond, built from super, over, and vivere, to live. The noun was formed in English in the sixteenth century; the older verb first meant to outlive someone, and the broader sense of staying alive came later.
intro.cn: 这个词来自动词「存活」，后者经盎格鲁法语从拉丁语 supervivere「活得超过」进入英语，由表示「在上、超过」的前缀与表示「活」的词根构成。名词在十六世纪的英语中形成；动词较早的意思是「比某人活得久」，后来才扩展到泛指「活着」。

items.en: Vivere meant to live, and it also stands behind vivid, vital and revive.
items.cn: 这个词意为活，也是「生动」「生命」「复活」等词的词根。

items.en: The prefix meant over, above or beyond.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为在上、超过、越过。

items.en: The verb meant to live beyond something or someone, literally to outlive.
items.cn: 这个动词意为活过某物或某人，字面就是「活得超过」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb north with the same comparative sense.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带向北方，保留同样的比较义。

items.en: English first used it for outliving a person, then for living through an event.
items.cn: 英语先用它指比某人活得久，后来指经历事件而活下来。

items.en: The noun was formed with the action ending; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词由表示行为的名词词尾构成，确切首见年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the living root or a derived ending; the second group names near equivalents for staying alive or lasting.
note.cn: 第一组共享「活」词根或派生词尾；第二组是表示「活着」或「持久」的近义说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to live through or outlive.
entries.definitionCN: 指经历……而活着或比……活得久的动词。

entries.definition: A person or thing that has lived through a danger.
entries.definitionCN: 指从危险中活下来的人或物。

entries.definition: Able to be lived through without death.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够活过来的、可幸存的。

entries.definition: The degree to which something can survive.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物能够存活的程度，即可存活程度。

entries.definition: A person who prepares for disaster or social collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 指为灾难或社会崩溃做准备的人。

entries.definition: The quality of continuing despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 指尽管困难仍持续下去的性质。

entries.definition: The ability to bear hardship for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 指长时间承受艰苦的能力。

entries.definition: Long life or long duration.
entries.definitionCN: 指长寿或持续时间长。

entries.definition: The ability to live, grow or continue successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 指存活、生长或成功持续的能力。

entries.definition: The bare fact of being, without the idea of threat.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在的单纯事实，不含威胁意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the root meaning to live beyond, and the many scales at which it applies.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着词根「活过、超过」展开，再想到它适用的多种尺度。

normal.en: Live plus over: to live past the thing that threatened you.
normal.cn: 活加超过：活过了威胁你的那件事。

normal.en: The oldest sense is outliving a person, not merely staying alive.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是比某人活得久，而不只是活着。

normal.en: A ceremony or a word can be a survival, a trace of an older world.
normal.cn: 一项仪式或一个词可以是残存物，是旧世界的痕迹。

normal.en: Hospitals count survival in rates over five years.
normal.cn: 医院以五年存活率来统计。

normal.en: Evolution cares about survival only insofar as it leads to offspring.
normal.cn: 演化只关心那些能带来后代的存活。

abstract.en: Survival is always measured against something: a threat, a deadline or another life.
abstract.cn: 存活总是相对某物来衡量：一个威胁、一个期限，或另一条生命。

abstract.en: What survives is not always what was strongest, only what kept going.
abstract.cn: 活下来的不总是最强者，只是继续下去的那一个。

abstract.en: Every institution speaks of survival in the language of biology.
abstract.cn: 每个机构都用生物学的语言谈自己的存续。

examples.en: The patient's survival depended on rapid surgery.
examples.cn: 病人的存活取决于及时手术。

examples.en: The custom is a survival from a time before written law.
examples.cn: 这一习俗是成文法之前时代的残存物。

examples.en: Long-term survival of the population requires connected habitats.
examples.cn: 种群的长期存续需要相互连通的栖息地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「色外涡」——「超过」加「活」，活过风雪就是幸存：幸存、生存

root: 动词经盎格鲁法语来自拉丁语 supervivere「活得超过」，由表示「在上、超过」的前缀与 vivere「活」构成；名词于十六世纪英语中形成，确切年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses range from simply staying alive to living through danger, outliving a person, a relic of the past, a statistical rate, evolutionary difference, a skill set, an organization's continuance, a species' persistence and a linguistic remnant.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从单纯活着出发，走向经历危险、比人活得久、旧时代残存物、统计存活率、演化差异、技能组合、机构存续、物种延续与语言遗留。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit window in a snowbound hut, a figure wrapped in blankets waiting for dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：风雪中小屋亮着的窗，一个裹着毯子等天亮的人。

branches.en: THE STATE AND THE THREAT: simply staying alive, and living through a danger.
branches.cn: 状态与威胁：单纯活着，以及闯过危险。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: living longer than another person.
branches.cn: 比较：比另一个人活得久。

branches.en: THE TRACE: a custom, object or word left from an older system.
branches.cn: 痕迹：旧系统留下的习俗、物件或词语。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND THE SELECTION: survival rates, and unequal survival in evolution.
branches.cn: 数字与选择：存活率，以及演化中的差别存活。

branches.en: THE SCALES: survival skills, an organization's continuance, and a species' persistence.
branches.cn: 尺度：生存技能、机构存续、物种延续。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of living-beyond with an English action ending; almost every derivative keeps the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「活得超过」的动词加英语行为词尾；几乎每个派生词都保留同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb to live and the prefix meaning over or beyond.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「活」的动词与表示「在上、超过」的前缀。

items.example: It is the root of survive, revive and vivid.
items.exampleCN: 它是「存活」「复活」「生动」等词的词根。

items.example: It gives the sense of living past something.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「活过某物」的意思。

items.example: Latin passed it through French to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语经法语把它传给英语。

items.example: The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。

items.example: It turns the verb into survival.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成「幸存」。

items.example: It forms survivor, one who lives through.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「幸存者」。

items.example: It forms survivable, able to be lived through.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可幸存的」。

items.example: It forms survivability, the degree of being survivable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可存活程度」。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁「活得超过」经法语构成，义为「活下来；比……活得久」
由动词加施动者词尾构成，义为「幸存者」
由动词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可幸存的」
由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「可存活程度」
由动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「残存的」
由「生存」加主张者词尾构成，义为「生存主义者」

definition_zh: 适者生存；最适应环境者存活下来（常被简化传播的说法）
definition_en: the principle that individuals best adapted to their environment are most likely to survive and reproduce, a phrase often simplified into a slogan
core_image: 草原上一群羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草
scene: 草原上一群羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草。In the wild, survival of the fittest is about leaving offspring, not about winning a fight.
sceneCN: 这里取第 4 个义项（「最适应」而非「最强」）；句意为在野外，适者生存讲的是留下后代，而不是打赢一场架。

pos.zh: 名词短语：适者生存；最适应环境者存活下来

collocations.phrase: the doctrine of survival of the fittest
a slogan of survival of the fittest
survival of the fittest in the market
a misuse of survival of the fittest
survival of the fittest among species
the phrase survival of the fittest

derivatives.zh: 由「适合的」加最高级词尾构成，义为「最适应的」
中古英语中义为「合适的、恰当的」，其更早来源不确定
由「适合的」加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「适应度；健康」
由「适合的」加比较级词尾构成，义为「更适应的」
由否定前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适合的」
