senses.title: A summary of natural selection
senses.definition: the principle that variants better suited to an environment leave more offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指更适应环境的变体留下更多后代这一原理
senses.example: Survival of the fittest summarises natural selection in five words.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」用五个词概括了自然选择。
senses.why: The phrase compresses a long argument into a memorable formula, which is both its strength and its danger.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语把长篇论证压成一句易记的口号，这既是它的力量，也是它的危险。

senses.title: Spencer's coinage
senses.definition: the phrase coined by Herbert Spencer in the eighteen-sixties after reading Darwin
senses.definitionCN: 指赫伯特·斯宾塞在十九世纪六十年代读达尔文之后造出的说法
senses.example: The phrase survival of the fittest was coined by Herbert Spencer.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」这一说法由赫伯特·斯宾塞造出。
senses.why: A philosopher of society supplied the words before the biologist adopted them.
senses.whyCN: 社会哲学家先提供了措辞，生物学家后来才采用。

senses.title: Darwin's adoption of the phrase
senses.titleCN: 达尔文对该短语的采用
senses.definition: the addition of the phrase to later editions of the Origin of Species as a synonym for natural selection
senses.definitionCN: 指达尔文在《物种起源》后来的版本中加入这条短语，作为自然选择的同义说法
senses.example: Darwin adopted survival of the fittest in the fifth edition.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文在第五版中采用了「适者生存」。
senses.why: Readers remembered the slogan more easily than the argument, so Darwin took it over.
senses.whyCN: 读者更容易记住口号而不是论证，达尔文于是把它收为己用。

senses.title: Fittest meaning best adapted
senses.definition: the sense that fit means suited to local conditions, not muscular or aggressive
senses.definitionCN: 指「适合」意为适应本地条件，而非肌肉强壮或好斗
senses.example: Survival of the fittest does not mean survival of the strongest.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」并不意味着最强者的生存。
senses.why: Fit is a relation between an organism and its surroundings, not a score in a fight.
senses.whyCN: 「适合」是生物与环境之间的关系，不是打斗的比分。

senses.title: The popular competitive misreading
senses.definition: the everyday use of the phrase to justify ruthless competition
senses.definitionCN: 指日常语言中用这条短语为无情竞争辩护
senses.example: The slogan survival of the fittest is often used to excuse ruthless competition.
senses.exampleCN: 「适者生存」这句口号常被用来为无情竞争开脱。
senses.why: A biological relation was turned into a social permission, and the turn is easy because the words sound like a race.
senses.whyCN: 一种生物关系被变成一种社会许可，这种转变之所以容易，是因为措辞听起来像一场赛跑。

senses.title: A business metaphor
senses.definition: the use of the phrase for firms competing and failing in a market
senses.definitionCN: 指用这条短语形容企业在市场中竞争与出局
senses.example: Executives invoke survival of the fittest to justify closures.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者援引「适者生存」为关厂辩护。
senses.why: Markets do select, but the selected unit is a firm, not a lineage, and the timescale is months, not generations.
senses.whyCN: 市场确实在选择，但被选择的单位是公司而非世系，时间尺度是几个月而非世代。

senses.title: Differential reproduction in ecology
senses.definition: the measurable version of the idea: which individuals leave the most surviving offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指这一想法的可测量版本：哪些个体留下最多存活后代
senses.example: Ecologists test survival of the fittest by counting offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家通过清点后代来检验「适者生存」。
senses.why: To be science rather than slogan, the phrase must be turned into counts and comparisons.
senses.whyCN: 要成为科学而非口号，这条短语必须变成计数与比较。

senses.title: Its misuse as social doctrine
senses.definition: the extension of the phrase to justify class, racial or national hierarchy
senses.definitionCN: 指把这条短语扩展到为阶级、种族或民族等级辩护
senses.example: Social Darwinism stretched survival of the fittest far beyond biology.
senses.exampleCN: 社会达尔文主义把「适者生存」远远扩展到生物学之外。
senses.why: The borrowing looked scientific while dropping every condition that made the original claim testable.
senses.whyCN: 这种借用看似科学，却丢掉了使原命题可检验的每一个条件。

senses.title: A critique of the phrase's limits
senses.definition: the objection that the slogan hides cooperation, luck and inheritance
senses.definitionCN: 指批评这句口号掩盖了合作、运气与遗传的作用
senses.example: Critics say survival of the fittest says little about cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说「适者生存」几乎没谈到合作。
senses.why: What a slogan leaves out is often what a theory most needs to explain.
senses.whyCN: 口号省略的部分，往往正是理论最需要解释的部分。

intro.en: The phrase is not ancient: Herbert Spencer coined it in the eighteen-sixties after reading Darwin, and Darwin adopted it in the fifth edition of the Origin of Species in 1869. Fit is an English adjective meaning suitable, first recorded in Middle English, and its earlier origin is uncertain; the superlative ending makes fittest mean most suited, not strongest.
intro.cn: 这条短语并不古老：赫伯特·斯宾塞在十九世纪六十年代读达尔文之后造出它，达尔文在一八六九年《物种起源》第五版中采用。「适合的」是英语形容词，中古英语已有记录，其更早来源不确定；最高级词尾使「最适」意为最适合，而非最强。

items.en: The adjective meant suitable or proper; its earlier origin is uncertain, and no Latin source can be assumed.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合适的、恰当的；其更早来源不确定，不能假定有拉丁语来源。

items.en: The superlative ending marks the highest degree of the quality.
items.cn: 这个最高级词尾标记性质的最高程度。

items.en: The first edition of the Origin argued for natural selection without using the slogan.
items.cn: 《物种起源》第一版论证自然选择，却没有使用这句口号。

items.en: Herbert Spencer coined the phrase in his biology, applying it to societies as well as organisms.
items.cn: 赫伯特·斯宾塞在其生物学著作中造出这条短语，并同时用于社会与生物。

items.en: Darwin added it to the fifth edition as a synonym, while Wallace disliked the substitution.
items.cn: 达尔文在第五版把它作为同义说法加入，而华莱士不喜欢这一替换。

items.en: The phrase spread as a slogan in business and politics, far from its original technical setting.
items.cn: 这条短语作为口号在商业与政治中传播，远离其原初的技术语境。

note.en: The first group shares the suitability word or a derived ending; the second group names the scientific concepts and the social misuse.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「适合」的词或派生词尾；第二组是科学概念与社会误用。

entries.definition: Suitable, in good condition, or a match of size and shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指合适的、健康的，或尺寸形状相合。

entries.definition: The superlative, most suited to the conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 最高级形式，指最适合条件。

entries.definition: The quality of being suitable, or good physical condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指适合的性质，或良好的体能。

entries.definition: Not suitable, or in poor condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指不适合的，或状态不佳的。

entries.definition: A person or thing that does not fit its surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 指与环境不合的人或物。

entries.definition: The process the phrase tries to summarise.
entries.definitionCN: 指这条短语试图概括的过程。

entries.definition: A trait that improves survival or reproduction in a setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在特定环境中改善存活或繁殖的性状。

entries.definition: In biology, the relative contribution to future generations.
entries.definitionCN: 生物学中指对未来世代的相对贡献。

entries.definition: Unequal survival among variants, the measurable core of the idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指变体之间不相等的存活，是这一想法的可测核心。

entries.definition: The misuse of biological selection to justify social hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 指把生物选择误用于为社会等级辩护。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations separate the phrase's three parts: who survives, what fit means, and who coined it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把短语分成三块：谁存活、「适合」指什么、以及是谁造的。

normal.en: Spencer coined it, Darwin adopted it, and Wallace disliked it.
normal.cn: 斯宾塞造出它，达尔文采用它，华莱士不喜欢它。

normal.en: Fit means suited to the place, not muscular or aggressive.
normal.cn: 「适合」指适应某地，而不是强壮或好斗。

normal.en: Success is measured in surviving offspring, not in victories.
normal.cn: 成功以存活后代来衡量，而不是以胜场。

normal.en: A firm is not a species, and a quarter is not a generation.
normal.cn: 公司不是物种，一个季度也不是一个世代。

normal.en: The slogan travels further than the theory because it is shorter.
normal.cn: 口号比理论传播得更远，因为它更短。

abstract.en: A memorable phrase can outrun the argument that gave it meaning.
abstract.cn: 一句易记的话，能跑得比赋予它意义的论证更远。

abstract.en: Selection is a relation to a place, not a ranking of strength.
abstract.cn: 选择是与某地的关系，而不是力量的排名。

abstract.en: Every slogan is a theory with its conditions stripped away.
abstract.cn: 每一句口号都是被剥掉条件的理论。

examples.en: Survival of the fittest is often printed on posters beside a picture of a race.
examples.cn: 「适者生存」常被印在海报上，旁边配一幅赛跑图。

examples.en: The phrase survival of the fittest entered biology through Spencer, not through Darwin's first edition.
examples.cn: 「适者生存」经由斯宾塞进入生物学，而不是通过达尔文的第一版。

examples.en: A market crash is not survival of the fittest in any biological sense.
examples.cn: 市场崩盘在任何生物学意义上都不是「适者生存」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「色外涡·欧夫·则·菲泰斯特」——活下来的是最「合身」的那个，不是最壮的那个：适者生存

root: 短语由十九世纪六十年代的斯宾塞造出，达尔文于一八六九年第五版采用；其中「适合的」是中古英语形容词，更早来源不确定，最高级词尾表示「最适合」，与「最强」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the phrase from its compressed scientific meaning to its coinage, Darwin's adoption, the true sense of fit, the popular misreading, the business metaphor, the ecological measure, the social misuse and the critique.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从被压缩的科学含义出发，走向它的造语、达尔文的采用、「适合」的真正含义、流行误读、商业比喻、生态测量、社会误用与批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: antelopes running, the laggard swallowed by dust, while a calf keeps grazing far off.
core.cn: 核心意象：羚羊奔逃，落后的一只被尘土吞没，远处的幼崽仍在吃草。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM AND ITS MEASURE: natural selection compressed, and the offspring counts that test it.
branches.cn: 机制与测量：被压缩的自然选择，以及检验它的后代计数。

branches.en: THE AUTHORSHIP: Spencer's coinage and Darwin's later adoption.
branches.cn: 作者：斯宾塞的造语与达尔文后来的采用。

branches.en: WHAT FIT MEANS: suited to local conditions, not strongest.
branches.cn: 「适合」的含义：适应本地条件，而非最强。

branches.en: THE POPULAR AND COMMERCIAL USES: an excuse for competition, and a market metaphor.
branches.cn: 流行与商业用法：为竞争开脱，以及市场比喻。

branches.en: THE MISUSE AND THE CRITIQUE: social hierarchy dressed as biology, and what the slogan hides.
branches.cn: 误用与批评：披着生物学外衣的社会等级，以及口号所掩盖的东西。

intro.en: The phrase is plain English grammar around one adjective: survival, of, the, fittest.
intro.cn: 这条短语是一个形容词加上普通的英语语法成分：生存、的、最、适合的。

latinIntro.en: Only survival has a Latin ancestry; the adjective fit is English, and its earlier source is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「生存」有拉丁语祖先；形容词「适合的」是英语词，其更早来源不确定。

items.example: Its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 其更早来源不确定。

items.example: It forms fittest, most suited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「最适合的」。

items.example: The word is about relation, not strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个词关乎关系，而非力量。

items.example: It supplies the first noun of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语的第一个名词。

items.example: It links survival to the group that survives.
items.exampleCN: 它把「存活」与存活的群体连接起来。

items.example: It makes fittest refer to a class rather than a person.
items.exampleCN: 它使「最适者」指一类而非某个人。

items.example: It underlies survival through the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 它经拉丁动词支撑「生存」一词。

items.example: It forms survival from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成「生存」。

derivatives.zh: 由「适合的」加最高级词尾构成，义为「最适合的」
中古英语义为「合适的」，更早来源不确定
由「适合的」加抽象名词词尾构成，义为「适应度」
由「适合的」加比较级词尾构成，义为「更适应的」
由否定前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适合的」
由表示「错误」的前缀加「适合的」构成，义为「不适应者」

definition_zh: 繁殖成效；繁殖成功率；留下存活后代的数量
definition_en: the number of offspring an individual produces that survive to reproduce, used as a measure of evolutionary fitness
core_image: 灌木丛里一只鸟反复衔虫回巢，巢中雏鸟张嘴待哺
scene: 灌木丛里一只鸟反复衔虫回巢，巢中雏鸟张嘴待哺。Reproductive success is counted in chicks that live long enough to breed.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（繁殖成效）；句意为繁殖成效以长到能繁殖的雏鸟数量来计算。

pos.zh: 名词短语：繁殖成效；繁殖成功率；存活后代数

derivatives.zh: 由「再」前缀加拉丁「引出、产生」动词构成，义为「繁殖；复制」
由动词加行为名词词尾构成，义为「繁殖；复制」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「繁殖的；生殖的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在繁殖方面」
由拉丁「随后到来、顺利发生」的动词构成，义为「成功；成效」
由「成功」加形容词词尾构成，义为「成功的」
由拉丁「随后到来」的动词经法语构成，义为「成功；继任」
由同一拉丁动词加名词词尾构成，义为「连续；继承」

senses.title: The number of surviving offspring
senses.definition: the count of offspring produced by an individual that themselves survive
senses.definitionCN: 指一个个体所产生并存活下来的后代数量
senses.example: Reproductive success is counted in chicks that live long enough to breed.
senses.exampleCN: 繁殖成效以长到能繁殖的雏鸟数量来计算。
senses.why: The phrase begins as a counting rule: not eggs laid, but young that live.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语最初是一条计数规则：不是下了多少蛋，而是活下来多少幼体。

senses.title: A proxy for evolutionary fitness
senses.titleCN: 演化适应度的替代指标
senses.definition: a practical stand-in for fitness, measured through descendants rather than genes
senses.definitionCN: 指适应度的实用替代，以后代而非基因来测量
senses.example: Field studies use reproductive success as a proxy for fitness.
senses.exampleCN: 野外研究用繁殖成效作为适应度的替代指标。
senses.why: Fitness is abstract; offspring are countable, so the phrase bridges theory and fieldwork.
senses.whyCN: 适应度是抽象的，后代是可数的，这条短语便在理论与野外工作之间搭桥。

senses.title: Lifetime reproductive success
senses.definition: the total offspring an individual produces over its whole life
senses.definitionCN: 指一个个体一生所产生后代的总数
senses.example: Lifetime reproductive success is recorded for every marked female.
senses.exampleCN: 每只被标记的雌性都记录终生繁殖成效。
senses.why: A single season can mislead, so the measure is extended to a whole life.
senses.whyCN: 单季数据可能误导，因此这一度量被扩展到整个一生。

senses.title: A variable in behavioural ecology
senses.titleCN: 行为生态学中的研究变量
senses.definition: the response variable in studies of mate choice, territory and parental care
senses.definitionCN: 指在配偶选择、领域与亲代抚育研究中的因变量
senses.example: The study tests how territory size affects reproductive success.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验领域大小如何影响繁殖成效。
senses.why: Once it is a variable, every behaviour can be asked whether it raises the count.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它成为变量，便可追问每一种行为是否提高这个数字。

senses.title: Seed or offspring output in plants
senses.titleCN: 植物的种子或后代产出
senses.definition: the plant equivalent: seeds produced, dispersed and established
senses.definitionCN: 指植物中的对应量：种子产生、散布并成功定植的数量
senses.example: In plants, reproductive success depends on pollinators and seed dispersal.
senses.exampleCN: 在植物中，繁殖成效取决于传粉者与种子散布。
senses.why: Plants cannot move to a mate, so their success is mediated by other species.
senses.whyCN: 植物不能走向配偶，因此它们的成效由其他物种来中介。

senses.title: Unequal variance between individuals
senses.definition: the fact that a few individuals may contribute many more offspring than others
senses.definitionCN: 指少数个体可能比其余个体留下多得多的后代
senses.example: Variance in reproductive success is higher among males in many species.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多物种中，雄性的繁殖成效差异更大。
senses.why: Selection needs difference, and the phrase measures how uneven the difference is.
senses.whyCN: 选择需要差异，这条短语衡量差异有多不均。

senses.title: A target in conservation breeding
senses.definition: the goal of producing offspring that survive and maintain genetic diversity
senses.definitionCN: 指产生能够存活并维持遗传多样性的后代这一目标
senses.example: The captive programme monitors reproductive success each season.
senses.exampleCN: 圈养繁育计划每季监测繁殖成效。
senses.why: In conservation, counting births is not enough; the young must survive and breed.
senses.whyCN: 在保护工作中，只数出生还不够，幼体必须存活并繁殖。

senses.title: The phrase as a reported statistic
senses.titleCN: 作为报告统计量的说法
senses.definition: a labelled number in a table or abstract, with a stated measure and period
senses.definitionCN: 指表格或摘要中带明确度量方式与时间段的标注数字
senses.example: The paper reports reproductive success as young fledged per pair.
senses.exampleCN: 论文以每对育出的雏鸟数报告繁殖成效。
senses.why: A number without its measure is meaningless, so the phrase always travels with a unit.
senses.whyCN: 没有度量方式的数字毫无意义，因此这条短语总是带着单位一起出现。

senses.title: Everyday use for breeding outcomes
senses.titleCN: 日常语境中的繁殖结果
senses.definition: a general way of saying that an animal or plant bred well or poorly
senses.definitionCN: 指笼统说明一种动植物繁殖得好或不好的说法
senses.example: Gardeners judge reproductive success by the seed they collect.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁以收得的种子来判断繁殖成效。
senses.why: The technical phrase leaks into ordinary speech, where it simply means a good breeding year.
senses.whyCN: 技术短语渗入日常语言，在那里只表示繁殖顺利的一年。

intro.en: Reproductive joins re-, again, with Latin producere, to lead forward, from ducere, to lead, plus the adjective ending -ive. Success comes from Latin successus, from succedere, to come next or go well, built from sub-, next to, and cedere, to go. The two words form a technical collocation of the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 「繁殖的」由表示「再」的前缀与拉丁语 producere「向前引出」构成，后者源于 ducere「引导」，再加形容词词尾。「成功」出自拉丁语 successus，源于 succedere「随后到来、顺利发生」，由表示「紧随」的前缀与 cedere「走」构成。两个词在二十世纪组合成技术短语。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or to draw along, the root of duct, conduct and produce.
items.cn: 这个词意为引导、牵引，是「管道」「传导」「产生」等词的词根。

items.en: Pro- forward plus ducere gave a verb meaning to lead out or bring forth.
items.cn: 表示「向前」的前缀加「引导」，构成意为「引出、产生」的动词。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or to yield, the root of proceed, recede and succeed.
items.cn: 这个词意为走、让步，是「前进」「退去」「成功」等词的词根。

items.en: Sub- next to plus cedere gave a verb meaning to come next, and then to turn out well.
items.cn: 表示「紧随」的前缀加「走」，构成意为「随后到来」、进而表示「顺利」的动词。

items.en: English took the noun for a favourable outcome and later for achieving a goal.
items.cn: 英语借入这个名词，先指有利结果，后指达成目标。

items.en: Biology combined the two words in the twentieth century as studies of selection became quantitative; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着选择研究变得定量化，生物学在二十世纪把两个词组合起来；确切首见时间不确定。

note.en: The first group shares a root or an ending; the second group names the measures and outcomes it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或词尾；第二组是与之比较的度量与结果。

entries.definition: The process of producing offspring or copies.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生后代或副本的过程。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 指与繁殖有关的形容词。

entries.definition: To produce offspring or make a copy.
entries.definitionCN: 指繁殖或复制。

entries.definition: A favourable outcome or the achievement of a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 指有利结果或达成目标。

entries.definition: Having achieved a desired result.
entries.definitionCN: 指已取得期望结果的。

entries.definition: The relative genetic contribution to future generations.
entries.definitionCN: 指对未来世代的相对遗传贡献。

entries.definition: The total offspring produced over a whole life.
entries.definitionCN: 指一生所产生后代的总数。

entries.definition: The potential number of offspring produced, before survival is counted.
entries.definitionCN: 指在计入存活之前的生产后代潜力。

entries.definition: The young produced by an individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个个体所产生的幼体。

entries.definition: Unequal reproduction among variants, the engine of selection.
entries.definitionCN: 指变体之间不相等的繁殖，是选择的引擎。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow what is counted: young that live, not eggs that are laid.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「数什么」展开：活下来的幼体，而不是产下的卵。

normal.en: Count the young that reach breeding age, not the eggs in the nest.
normal.cn: 数长到能繁殖的幼体，而不是巢里的卵。

normal.en: Lifetime reproductive success adds up every season of one life.
normal.cn: 终生繁殖成效把一个生命的每个季节都加起来。

normal.en: In plants the count is seeds that establish, not seeds that fall.
normal.cn: 在植物中，数的是成功定植的种子，而不是落下的种子。

normal.en: High variance means a few individuals contribute most of the next generation.
normal.cn: 差异大意味着少数个体贡献了下一代的大部分。

normal.en: In conservation, births must be followed by survival and breeding.
normal.cn: 在保护工作中，出生之后还必须存活并繁殖。

abstract.en: Success in evolution is not fame or size; it is representation in the next generation.
abstract.cn: 演化中的成功不是名声或体型，而是在下一代中的代表性。

abstract.en: A measure must name its unit, or it measures nothing.
abstract.cn: 度量必须说明单位，否则什么也没测到。

abstract.en: Selection is statistics played out in bodies.
abstract.cn: 选择是写在身体上的统计学。

examples.en: The study links song complexity to reproductive success in male birds.
examples.cn: 这项研究把鸣唱复杂度与雄鸟的繁殖成效联系起来。

examples.en: Lifetime reproductive success varies widely among females in this population.
examples.cn: 这个种群中雌性的终生繁殖成效差异很大。

examples.en: Pollinator loss reduced reproductive success in the orchid.
examples.cn: 传粉者减少使这种兰花的繁殖成效下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞普罗达克提夫·萨克塞斯」——再「引出」后代并且成功养大，就是繁殖成效

root: 「繁殖的」由表示「再」的前缀与拉丁语 producere「向前引出」（源于 ducere「引导」）加形容词词尾构成；「成功」出自拉丁语 successus「顺利到来」（源于 succedere，由「紧随」前缀与 cedere「走」构成）；短语为二十世纪技术组合，确切首见时间不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a simple count of surviving young to a fitness proxy, a lifetime total, a study variable, plant output, variance, a conservation goal, a reported statistic and everyday usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「数活下来的幼体」出发，走向适应度替代、终生总数、研究变量、植物产出、差异程度、保护目标、报告统计量与日常用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird ferrying insects to a nest, chicks with open beaks waiting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鸟反复把虫子衔回巢，雏鸟张着嘴等食。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND ITS UNIT: surviving young, and the labelled statistic in a report.
branches.cn: 计数与单位：存活的幼体，以及报告中带单位的统计量。

branches.en: THE PROXY AND THE LIFETIME: fitness measured through descendants, summed over a life.
branches.cn: 替代与终生：以后代测量适应度，并把一生加总。

branches.en: THE VARIABLE AND THE VARIANCE: behaviour studies, and unequal contributions.
branches.cn: 变量与差异：行为研究，以及不相等的贡献。

branches.en: THE PLANT VERSION: seeds that disperse and establish.
branches.cn: 植物版本：散布并成功定植的种子。

branches.en: THE APPLIED AND THE EVERYDAY: conservation breeding targets, and ordinary breeding outcomes.
branches.cn: 应用与日常：保护繁育目标，以及日常的繁殖结果。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of leading forward with a Latin verb of coming next, each wearing an English ending.
intro.cn: 这条短语把拉丁语「向前引出」的动词与「随后到来」的动词连在一起，各自带着英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both verbs and both prefixes: again and forward for the first word, next to for the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供两个动词与两个前缀：第一个词是「再」与「向前」，第二个词是「紧随」。

items.example: It gives the sense of producing again.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「再次产生」的意思。

items.example: It is the root of produce and duct.
items.exampleCN: 它是「产生」与「管道」等词的词根。

items.example: It is the source of reproduce.
items.exampleCN: 它是「繁殖」一词的来源。

items.example: It forms reproductive from reproduction.
items.exampleCN: 它由「繁殖」构成「繁殖的」。

items.example: It gives the sense of coming next.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「紧随其后」的意思。

items.example: It is the root of succeed and proceed.
items.exampleCN: 它是「成功」与「前进」等词的词根。

items.meaning: to come next, turn out well
items.example: It is the source of success.
items.exampleCN: 它是「成功」一词的来源。

items.example: The noun supplies the second half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供短语的后半部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to come next, turn out well

derivatives.zh: 由「再」前缀加拉丁「向前引出」动词构成，义为「繁殖」
由动词加行为名词词尾构成，义为「繁殖」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「繁殖的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在繁殖方面」
由拉丁「顺利到来」名词构成，义为「成功」
由「成功」加形容词词尾构成，义为「成功的」
由拉丁「随后到来」动词经法语构成，义为「成功」
由同一拉丁动词加名词词尾构成，义为「连续；继承」
